1.70.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
atha vakṣye mahāviṣṇormantrānlokeṣu durlabhān /
yānprāpya mānavāstūrṇaṃ prāpnuvanti nijepsitam //
1.70.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
अथ वक्ष्ये महाविष्णोर्मन्त्रान्लोकेषु दुर्लभान् ।
यान्प्राप्य मानवास्तूर्णं प्राप्नुवन्ति निजेप्सितम् ॥
1.70.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Now I shall declare the mantras of Mahāviṣṇu, difficult to obtain in the worlds, / having attained which, men quickly accomplish their desired end.

1.70.s:
yeṣāmuñcāraṇeneva pāpasaṃghaḥ pralīyate /
brahmādayo 'pi yāñjñātvā samarthāḥ syurjagatkṛtau //
1.70.d:
येषामुञ्चारणेनेव पापसंघः प्रलीयते ।
ब्रह्मादयो ऽपि याञ्ज्ञात्वा समर्थाः स्युर्जगत्कृतौ ॥
1.70.m: By the mere utterance of which the mass of sins dissolves, / and having known which even Brahmā and the others become capable of creating the world;

1.70.s:
tārahṛtpūrvakaṃ ṅeṃtaṃ nārāyaṇapadaṃ bhavet /
aṣṭākṣaro manuścāsya sādhyo nārāyaṇo muniḥ //
1.70.d:
तारहृत्पूर्वकं ङेंतं नारायणपदं भवेत् ।
अष्टाक्षरो मनुश्चास्य साध्यो नारायणो मुनिः ॥
1.70.m: preceded by the tāra and hṛt, let the word 'Nārāyaṇa' end in the dative: / this is the eight-syllabled mantra, whose master-seer is the sage Nārāyaṇa;

1.70.s:
chandaḥ proktaṃ ca gāyatrī devatā viṣṇukhyayaḥ /
oṃ bījaṃ yaṃ ca tathā śaktirviniyogo 'khilāptaye //
1.70.d:
छन्दः प्रोक्तं च गायत्री देवता विष्णुख्ययः ।
ओं बीजं यं च तथा शक्तिर्विनियोगो ऽखिलाप्तये ॥
1.70.m: its meter is said to be the gāyatrī, and the deity is named Viṣṇu; / 'Oṃ' is the seed-syllable, and 'yaṃ' is the energy; its ritual application is for the attainment of all ends.

1.70.s:
kruddholkāya hṛdākhyātaṃ maholkāya śiraḥ smṛtam /
vīrolkāya śikhā proktā dyulkāya kavacaṃ matam //
1.70.d:
क्रुद्धोल्काय हृदाख्यातं महोल्काय शिरः स्मृतम् ।
वीरोल्काय शिखा प्रोक्ता द्युल्काय कवचं मतम् ॥
1.70.m: 'To Kruddholka' is declared the heart; 'To Maholka' is recorded the head; / 'To Vīrolka' is said the topknot; 'To Dyulkay' is deemed the armour;

1.70.s:
maholkāyeti cāsraṃ syāditthaṃ pañcāṅgakalpanā /
punaḥ ṣaḍaṅgamantrotthaiḥ ṣaḍvarṇaiśca samācaret //
1.70.d:
महोल्कायेति चास्रं स्यादित्थं पञ्चाङ्गकल्पना ।
पुनः षडङ्गमन्त्रोत्थैः षड्वर्णैश्च समाचरेत् ॥
1.70.m: and 'To Maholka' is the weapon: such is the arrangement of the five limbs. / Then one should also perform [the nyāsa] with the six syllables arising from the six-limbed mantra;

1.70.s:
avaśiṣṭau nyasetkukṣipṛṣṭayormantravarṇakau /
sudarśanasya mantreṇa kuryāddigbandhanaṃ tataḥ //
1.70.d:
अवशिष्टौ न्यसेत्कुक्षिपृष्टयोर्मन्त्रवर्णकौ ।
सुदर्शनस्य मन्त्रेण कुर्याद्दिग्बन्धनं ततः ॥
1.70.m: one should place the two remaining mantra-syllables on the belly and back; / then one should perform the sealing of the directions with the mantra of Sudarśana.

1.70.s:
tāro namaścaturthyantaṃ sudarśanapadaṃ vadet /
astrāyaphaḍiti prokto mantro dvādaśavarṇavān //
1.70.d:
तारो नमश्चतुर्थ्यन्तं सुदर्शनपदं वदेत् ।
अस्त्रायफडिति प्रोक्तो मन्त्रो द्वादशवर्णवान् ॥
1.70.m: One should utter the tāra, 'namaḥ', the word 'Sudarśana' ending in the dative, / and 'astrāya phaṭ': [thus] the twelve-syllabled mantra is proclaimed.

1.70.s:
daśāvṛttimaya nyāsaṃ vakṣye vibhūtipañcaram /
mūlārṇānsvatanau nyasyedādhāre hṛdaye mukhe //
1.70.d:
दशावृत्तिमय न्यासं वक्ष्ये विभूतिपञ्चरम् ।
मूलार्णान्स्वतनौ न्यस्येदाधारे हृदये मुखे ॥
1.70.m: I shall state the nyāsa consisting of ten repetitions, called the vibhūtipañjara: / one should place the root syllables upon one's own body—at the base, the heart, the mouth,

1.70.s:
doḥpanmūleṣu nāsāyāṃ prathamāvṛttirīritā /
gale nābhau hṛdi kucapārśvapṛṣṭeṣu tatparāḥ //
1.70.d:
दोःपन्मूलेषु नासायां प्रथमावृत्तिरीरिता ।
गले नाभौ हृदि कुचपार्श्वपृष्टेषु तत्पराः ॥
1.70.m: at the base of the arms and feet, and in the nose: this is stated as the first repetition; / in the throat, navel, heart, breast, sides, and back are the next;

1.70.s:
mūrddhāsyanetraśravaṇaghrāṇeṣu ca tṛtīyakāḥ /
doḥpādasaṃdhyaṅguliṣu vedāvṛttyā ca vinyaset //
1.70.d:
मूर्द्धास्यनेत्रश्रवणघ्राणेषु च तृतीयकाः ।
दोःपादसंध्यङ्गुलिषु वेदावृत्त्या च विन्यसेत् ॥
1.70.m: on the crown of the head, the mouth, the eyes, ears, and nose are the third; / and on the joints and fingers and toes of the arms and feet one should place them in the fourth repetition;

1.70.s:
dhātuprāṇeṣu hṛdaye vinyasettadanantaram /
śironetrā syahṛtkukṣisorujaṅghāpadadvaye //
1.70.d:
धातुप्राणेषु हृदये विन्यसेत्तदनन्तरम् ।
शिरोनेत्रा स्यहृत्कुक्षिसोरुजङ्घापदद्वये ॥
1.70.m: thereafter one should place them on the bodily elements, the vital breaths, and the heart; / on the head, eyes, mouth, heart, belly, thighs, shanks, and both feet,

1.70.s:
ekaikaśo nyasedvarṇānmantrasya kramataḥ sudhīḥ /
nyaseddhṛdaṃsorupadeṣvarṇānvedamitānmanoḥ //
1.70.d:
एकैकशो न्यसेद्वर्णान्मन्त्रस्य क्रमतः सुधीः ।
न्यसेद्धृदंसोरुपदेष्वर्णान्वेदमितान्मनोः ॥
1.70.m: the wise one should place the syllables of the mantra one by one in succession; / one should place the four syllables of the mantra on the heart, shoulders, thighs, and feet;

1.70.s:
cakraśaṃ khagadāṃbhojapadeṣu svasvamudrayā /
śeṣāṃśca nyāsavaryo 'yaṃ vibhūtipañjarābhidhaḥ //
1.70.d:
चक्रशं खगदांभोजपदेषु स्वस्वमुद्रया ।
शेषांश्च न्यासवर्यो ऽयं विभूतिपञ्जराभिधः ॥
1.70.m: and with each one's own hand-gesture upon the positions of the discus, conch, mace, and lotus, / and the rest: this is the foremost nyāsa, named vibhūtipañjara.

1.70.s:
nyasenmūlārṇamekaikaṃ sacandraṃ tārasampuṭam /
athavā vai namontena nyasedityapare jaguḥ //
1.70.d:
न्यसेन्मूलार्णमेकैकं सचन्द्रं तारसम्पुटम् ।
अथवा वै नमोन्तेन न्यसेदित्यपरे जगुः ॥
1.70.m: One should place each root syllable with a crescent moon, enveloped by the tāra; / or else, one should place them ending in 'namaḥ', so others have proclaimed.

1.70.s:
tattvanyāsaṃ tataḥ kuryāddhiṣṇubhāvaprasiddhaye /
aṣṭārṇo 'ṣṭaprakṛtyātmā gaditaḥ pūrvasūribhiḥ //
1.70.d:
तत्त्वन्यासं ततः कुर्याद्धिष्णुभावप्रसिद्धये ।
अष्टार्णो ऽष्टप्रकृत्यात्मा गदितः पूर्वसूरिभिः ॥
1.70.m: Then one should perform the tattvanyāsa for the realization of the state of Viṣṇu: / the eight-syllabled [mantra] is declared by ancient sages to consist of the eight primary principles;

1.70.s:
pṛthivyādīni bhūtāni tato 'hṝṅkārameva ca /
mahāṃśca prakṛtiścaivetyaṣṭau prakṛtayo matāḥ //
1.70.d:
पृथिव्यादीनि भूतानि ततो ऽहॄङ्कारमेव च ।
महांश्च प्रकृतिश्चैवेत्यष्टौ प्रकृतयो मताः ॥
1.70.m: the elements beginning with earth, then the 'I'-maker, / the intellect, and primordial matter: these are considered the eight primary principles.

1.70.s:
pāde liṅge hṛdi mukhe mūrdhni vakṣasi hṛtsthale /
sarvāṅge vyāpakaṃ kuryādekena sādhakottamaḥ //
1.70.d:
पादे लिङ्गे हृदि मुखे मूर्ध्नि वक्षसि हृत्स्थले ।
सर्वाङ्गे व्यापकं कुर्यादेकेन साधकोत्तमः ॥
1.70.m: On the foot, the phallus, the heart, the mouth, the crown of the head, the chest, the region of the heart, / and over all limbs as an all-pervading [nyāsa], the foremost practitioner should perform [it] with one [syllable];

1.70.s:
mantrārṇahṛtparāyādyamātmane hṛdayāntimam /
tattannāma samuñcāryya nyasettattatsthale budhaḥ //
1.70.d:
मन्त्रार्णहृत्परायाद्यमात्मने हृदयान्तिमम् ।
तत्तन्नाम समुञ्चार्य्य न्यसेत्तत्तत्स्थले बुधः ॥
1.70.m: with the mantra-syllable, 'hṛt', 'parāya', and beginning with 'ātmane' and ending with 'hṛdayāya', / having uttered the respective name, the wise one should place [them] on each respective spot.

1.70.s:
ayaṃ tattvābhidho nyāsaḥ sarvanyāsottamottamaḥ /
mūrtīnyaṃseddvādaśa vai dvādaśādityasaṃyutāḥ //
1.70.d:
अयं तत्त्वाभिधो न्यासः सर्वन्यासोत्तमोत्तमः ।
मूर्तीन्यंसेद्द्वादश वै द्वादशादित्यसंयुताः ॥
1.70.m: This is the nyāsa named tattva, the most supreme of all nyāsas; / one should indeed place the twelve forms, united with the twelve Ādityas,

1.70.s:
dvādaśākṣaravarṇādyā dvādaśādityasaṃyutāḥ /
aṣṭārṇo 'yaṃ manuścāṣṭaprakṛtyātmā samīritaḥ //
1.70.d:
द्वादशाक्षरवर्णाद्या द्वादशादित्यसंयुताः ।
अष्टार्णो ऽयं मनुश्चाष्टप्रकृत्यात्मा समीरितः ॥
1.70.m: beginning with the letters of the twelve-syllabled mantra, united with the twelve Ādityas; / and this eight-syllabled mantra is proclaimed to consist of the eight primary principles;

1.70.s:
tāsāmātmacatuṣkasya yogādarkākṣaro bhavet /
lalāṭakukṣihṛtkaṇṭhadakṣapārśvāṃsakeṣu ca //
1.70.d:
तासामात्मचतुष्कस्य योगादर्काक्षरो भवेत् ।
ललाटकुक्षिहृत्कण्ठदक्षपार्श्वांसकेषु च ॥
1.70.m: by uniting their four selves, it becomes the twelve-syllabled [mantra]; / on the forehead, belly, heart, throat, right side, and right shoulder,

1.70.s:
gale ca vāmapārśvāṃ sagalapṛṣṭeṣvanantaram /
kakudyapi nyasenmantrī mūrtīrdvādaśa vai kramāt //
1.70.d:
गले च वामपार्श्वां सगलपृष्टेष्वनन्तरम् ।
ककुद्यपि न्यसेन्मन्त्री मूर्तीर्द्वादश वै क्रमात् ॥
1.70.m: and on the throat, left side, left shoulder, the back of the neck, / and on the hump of the neck, the practitioner of mantras should place the twelve forms in sequence:

1.70.s:
dhātrā tu keśavaṃ nyasyāryamṇa nārāyaṇaṃ punaḥ /
mitreṇa mādhavaṃ nyasya govindaṃ varuṇena ca //
1.70.d:
धात्रा तु केशवं न्यस्यार्यम्ण नारायणं पुनः ।
मित्रेण माधवं न्यस्य गोविन्दं वरुणेन च ॥
1.70.m: having placed Keśava with Dhātṛ, and then Nārāyaṇa with Aryaman, / having placed Mādhava with Mitra, and Govinda with Varuṇa,

1.70.s:
viṣṇuṃ caivāṃśunā yuktaṃ bhagena madhusūdanam /
nyasedvivasvatā yuktaṃ trivikramamataḥ param //
1.70.d:
विष्णुं चैवांशुना युक्तं भगेन मधुसूदनम् ।
न्यसेद्विवस्वता युक्तं त्रिविक्रममतः परम् ॥
1.70.m: and Viṣṇu joined with Aṃśu, Madhusūdana with Bhaga, / after that one should place Trivikrama joined with Vivasvat,

1.70.s:
vāmanaṃ ca tathādraṇa pūṣṇā śrīdharameva ca /
hṛṣīkeśaṃ nyasetpaścātparjanyena samanvitam //
1.70.d:
वामनं च तथाद्रण पूष्णा श्रीधरमेव च ।
हृषीकेशं न्यसेत्पश्चात्पर्जन्येन समन्वितम् ॥
1.70.m: and likewise Vāmana with Indra, and Śrīdhara with Pūṣan, / and then one should place Hṛṣīkeśa joined with Parjanya,

1.70.s:
tvaṣṭrā yutaṃ padmanābhaṃ dāmodaraṃ ca viṣṇunā /
dvādasārṇaṃ tato mantraṃ samaste śirasi nyaset //
1.70.d:
त्वष्ट्रा युतं पद्मनाभं दामोदरं च विष्णुना ।
द्वादसार्णं ततो मन्त्रं समस्ते शिरसि न्यसेत् ॥
1.70.m: Padmanābha accompanied by Tvaṣṭṛ, and Dāmodara with Viṣṇu; / then one should place the entire twelve-syllabled mantra upon the head.

1.70.s:
vyāpakaṃ vinyasetpaścātkirīṭamanunā sudhīḥ /
dhruvaḥkirīṭakeyūrahārānte makaretica //
1.70.d:
व्यापकं विन्यसेत्पश्चात्किरीटमनुना सुधीः ।
ध्रुवःकिरीटकेयूरहारान्ते मकरेतिच ॥
1.70.m: Then the wise one should perform an all-pervading placement with the kirīṭa-mantra: / the dhruva, followed by 'kirīṭakeyūrahāra', then 'makara',

1.70.s:
kuṇḍalānte cakraśaṅkhagadānteṃ'bhojahastataḥ /
pītāṃbarānte śrīvatsāṃ kitavakṣaḥ sthaleti ca //
1.70.d:
कुण्डलान्ते चक्रशङ्खगदान्तेंऽभोजहस्ततः ।
पीतांबरान्ते श्रीवत्सां कितवक्षः स्थलेति च ॥
1.70.m: after 'kuṇḍala', followed by 'cakraśaṅkhagadā', then 'ambojahastāya', / followed by 'pītāmbara', and 'śrīvatsāṅkitavakṣasthalāya',

1.70.s:
śrībhūmisahitasvātmajyotirdvayamataḥ param /
vadeddīptikarāyānti sahasrādityatejase //
1.70.d:
श्रीभूमिसहितस्वात्मज्योतिर्द्वयमतः परम् ।
वदेद्दीप्तिकरायान्ति सहस्रादित्यतेजसे ॥
1.70.m: then 'śrībhūmisahitasvātmajyotirdvayāya', / and one should utter 'dīptikarāya', and 'sahasrādityatejase',

1.70.s:
namonto bāṇaṣaṅvarṇaiḥ kirīṭamanurīritaḥ /
evaṃ nyāsavidhiṃ kṛtvā dhyāyennārāyaṇaṃ vibhum //
1.70.d:
नमोन्तो बाणषङ्वर्णैः किरीटमनुरीरितः ।
एवं न्यासविधिं कृत्वा ध्यायेन्नारायणं विभुम् ॥
1.70.m: ending in 'namaḥ', containing thirty-five syllables: thus is the kirīṭa-mantra proclaimed; / having performed the rite of nyāsa in this manner, one should meditate on the all-pervading Nārāyaṇa,

1.70.s:
udyatkoṭyarkasadṛśaṃ śaṅkhaṃ cakraṃ gadāṃbujam /
dadhataṃ ca karairbhūmiśrībhyāṃ pārśvadvayāñcitam //
1.70.d:
उद्यत्कोट्यर्कसदृशं शङ्खं चक्रं गदांबुजम् ।
दधतं च करैर्भूमिश्रीभ्यां पार्श्वद्वयाञ्चितम् ॥
1.70.m: who resembles ten million rising suns, holding the conch, discus, mace, and lotus / with his hands, flanked on both sides by Bhūmi and Śrī,

1.70.s:
śrīvatsavakṣasaṃ bhrājatkaustubhāmuktakandharam /
hārakeyūravalayāṅgadaṃ pītāṃbaraṃ smaret //
1.70.d:
श्रीवत्सवक्षसं भ्राजत्कौस्तुभामुक्तकन्धरम् ।
हारकेयूरवलयाङ्गदं पीतांबरं स्मरेत् ॥
1.70.m: having the Śrīvatsa on his chest, with the glistening Kaustubha adorning his neck; / one should remember him wearing yellow garments, adorned with necklaces, armlets, bracelets, and angadas.

1.70.s:
varṇalakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ vidhivanniyatendriyaḥ /
prathamena tu lakṣeṇa svātmaśuddhirbhaved dhruvam //
1.70.d:
वर्णलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं विधिवन्नियतेन्द्रियः ।
प्रथमेन तु लक्षेण स्वात्मशुद्धिर्भवेद् ध्रुवम् ॥
1.70.m: With senses controlled, one should recite the mantra according to rule for a hundred thousand times; / by the first hundred thousand, purification of one's own self is certain to occur;

1.70.s:
lakṣadvayajapenātha mantraśuddhimavāpnuyāt /
lakṣatrayeṇa japtena svarlokamadhigacchati //
1.70.d:
लक्षद्वयजपेनाथ मन्त्रशुद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ।
लक्षत्रयेण जप्तेन स्वर्लोकमधिगच्छति ॥
1.70.m: then by the recitation of two hundred thousand, one would attain purity of the mantra; / by three hundred thousand recited, one reaches the heavenly realm;

1.70.s:
viṣṇoḥ samīpamāpnoti vedalakṣajapānnaraḥ /
tathā ca nirmalaṃ jñānaṃ pañcalakṣajapādbhavet //
1.70.d:
विष्णोः समीपमाप्नोति वेदलक्षजपान्नरः ।
तथा च निर्मलं ज्ञानं पञ्चलक्षजपाद्भवेत् ॥
1.70.m: from the recitation of four hundred thousand, a man attains proximity to Viṣṇu; / and likewise, stainless knowledge arises from the recitation of five hundred thousand;

1.70.s:
lakṣaṣaṣṭena cāpnoti mantrī viṣṇau1sthirā matim /
saptalakṣajapānmantrī viṣṇoḥ sārūpyamāpnuyāt //
1.70.d:
लक्षषष्टेन चाप्नोति मन्त्री विष्णौ1स्थिरा मतिम् ।
सप्तलक्षजपान्मन्त्री विष्णोः सारूप्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
1.70.m: by six hundred thousand, the practitioner of mantras attains a firm mind fixed upon Viṣṇu; / from the recitation of seven hundred thousand, the practitioner of mantras would attain conformity of form with Viṣṇu;

1.70.s:
aṣṭalakṣaṃ japenmantrī nirvāṇamadhigacchati /
evaṃ japtvā tataḥ prājño daśāṃśaṃ sarasīruhaiḥ //
1.70.d:
अष्टलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्री निर्वाणमधिगच्छति ।
एवं जप्त्वा ततः प्राज्ञो दशांशं सरसीरुहैः ॥
1.70.m: the practitioner of mantras who recites eight hundred thousand attains absolute cessation; / having thus recited, the wise one should then offer in oblations a tenth part [of that] with lotuses

1.70.s:
madhurāktaiḥ prajuhuyātsaṃskṛte havyavāhane /
maṇḍūkātparatatvāntaṃ pīṭhe saṃpūjya yatnataḥ //
1.70.d:
मधुराक्तैः प्रजुहुयात्संस्कृते हव्यवाहने ।
मण्डूकात्परतत्वान्तं पीठे संपूज्य यत्नतः ॥
1.70.m: smeared with sweets into consecrated fire; / having worshiped with care on the ritual seat [all principles] from Maṇḍūka up to the Supreme Principle:

1.70.s:
vimalotkarṣiṇī jñānā kriyā yogā tataḥ parā /
prahvī satyā tatheśānanugrahā navamī matā //
1.70.d:
विमलोत्कर्षिणी ज्ञाना क्रिया योगा ततः परा ।
प्रह्वी सत्या तथेशाननुग्रहा नवमी मता ॥
1.70.m: Vimalā, Utkarṣiṇī, Jñānā, Kriyā, and thereafter Yogā, / Prahvī, Satyā, likewise Īśānā, and Anugrahā is considered the ninth;

1.70.s:
tāro namano bhagavate viṣṇave sarvabhū tataḥ /
tātmane vāsudevāya sarvātmeti padaṃ vadet //
1.70.d:
तारो नमनो भगवते विष्णवे सर्वभू ततः ।
तात्मने वासुदेवाय सर्वात्मेति पदं वदेत् ॥
1.70.m: the tāra, 'namo bhagavate viṣṇave', then 'sarvabhū-', / '-tātmane vāsudevāya', and one should utter the phrase 'sarvātma-';

1.70.s:
saṃyogayogapadmānte pīṭhāya hṛdayāntimaḥ /
ṣaḍviṃśadakṣaraḥ pīṭhamantro 'nenāsanaṃ diśet //
1.70.d:
संयोगयोगपद्मान्ते पीठाय हृदयान्तिमः ।
षड्विंशदक्षरः पीठमन्त्रो ऽनेनासनं दिशेत् ॥
1.70.m: ending in '-saṃyogayogapadmāya', ending with 'pīṭhāya' and 'hṛt': / this is the twenty-six-syllabled pīṭha-mantra; by this one should offer the seat.

1.70.s:
mūrtiṃ saṃkalpya mūlena tasyāmāvāhya pūjayet /
ādau cāṅgāni saṃpūjya mantrāṇāṃ keśareṣu ca //
1.70.d:
मूर्तिं संकल्प्य मूलेन तस्यामावाह्य पूजयेत् ।
आदौ चाङ्गानि संपूज्य मन्त्राणां केशरेषु च ॥
1.70.m: Having mentally formed the image, having invoked him into it with the root mantra, one should worship him; / and having first worshiped the limbs and the mantras upon the filaments,

1.70.s:
prāgādidigdale vāsudevaṃ saṃkarṣaṇaṃ tathā /
pradyumnamaniruddhaṃ ca śaktīḥ koṇeṣvathārcayet //
1.70.d:
प्रागादिदिग्दले वासुदेवं संकर्षणं तथा ।
प्रद्युम्नमनिरुद्धं च शक्तीः कोणेष्वथार्चयेत् ॥
1.70.m: on the petals in the directions beginning with the east [one should worship] Vāsudeva, Saṃkarṣaṇa, / Pradyumna, and Aniruddha; then one should worship the energies in the corners:

1.70.s:
śāntiṃ śriyaṃ sarasvatyā ratiṃ saṃpūjayetkramāt /
hemapītatamālendranīlābhāḥ pītavāsasaḥ //
1.70.d:
शान्तिं श्रियं सरस्वत्या रतिं संपूजयेत्क्रमात् ।
हेमपीततमालेन्द्रनीलाभाः पीतवाससः ॥
1.70.m: in sequence one should worship Śānti, Śrī, Sarasvatī, and Rati, / who have the luster of golden yellow, the tamāla tree, and the sapphire, and wear yellow garments,

1.70.s:
caturbhujāḥ śaṅkhacakragadāṃbhaghojadharā ime /
sitakāñcanagodugdhadūrvāvarṇāśca śaktayaḥ //
1.70.d:
चतुर्भुजाः शङ्खचक्रगदांभघोजधरा इमे ।
सितकाञ्चनगोदुग्धदूर्वावर्णाश्च शक्तयः ॥
1.70.m: possessing four arms, bearing the conch, discus, mace, and lotus; / and these energies have the colors of white, gold, cow's milk, and dūrvā grass.

1.70.s:
dalāgreṣu cakraśaṅkhagadāpaṅkajakaustubhān /
pūjayenmusalaṃ khaḍgaṃ vanamālāṃ yathākramāt //
1.70.d:
दलाग्रेषु चक्रशङ्खगदापङ्कजकौस्तुभान् ।
पूजयेन्मुसलं खड्गं वनमालां यथाक्रमात् ॥
1.70.m: On the tips of the petals one should worship in due order the discus, conch, mace, lotus, and Kaustubha, / the pestle, the sword, and the forest garland,

1.70.s:
raktājapītakanakaśyāmakṛṣṇāsitārjunān /
kuṅkumābhaṃ samabhyarcyedvahiragre khageśvaram //
1.70.d:
रक्ताजपीतकनकश्यामकृष्णासितार्जुनान् ।
कुङ्कुमाभं समभ्यर्च्येद्वहिरग्रे खगेश्वरम् ॥
1.70.m: colored red, yellow, dark green, black, dark, and white; / having worshiped the saffron-hued king of birds outside in front,

1.70.s:
pārśvayoḥ pūjayetpaścāṅkhapadmanidhī kramāt /
muktāmāṇikyasaṃkāśau paścime dhvajamaparcayet //
1.70.d:
पार्श्वयोः पूजयेत्पश्चाङ्खपद्मनिधी क्रमात् ।
मुक्तामाणिक्यसंकाशौ पश्चिमे ध्वजमपर्चयेत् ॥
1.70.m: one should then worship the Conch and Lotus treasures on both sides in order, / resembling pearls and rubies, and in the west one should worship the banner.

1.70.s:
raktaṃ vighnaṃ tathāgneye śyāmamāryaṃ ca rākṣase /
durgāṃ śyāmāṃ vāyukoṇe senānyaṃ pītamaiśvare //
1.70.d:
रक्तं विघ्नं तथाग्नेये श्याममार्यं च राक्षसे ।
दुर्गां श्यामां वायुकोणे सेनान्यं पीतमैश्वरे ॥
1.70.m: Likewise, the wise one should worship red Vighna in the south-east, dark Ārya in the south-west, / dark Durgā in the north-west, and yellow Senānī in the north-east.

1.70.s:
lokeśā nāyudhairyuktānbahiḥ saṃpūjayetsudhīḥ /
evamāvaraṇairyuktaṃ yor'cajayedviṣṇumavyayam //
1.70.d:
लोकेशा नायुधैर्युक्तान्बहिः संपूजयेत्सुधीः ।
एवमावरणैर्युक्तं योर्ऽचजयेद्विष्णुमव्ययम् ॥
1.70.m: On the outside, the wise one should worship the lords of the worlds equipped with their weapons. / Whoever worships the imperishable Viṣṇu surrounded by enclosures in this manner,

1.70.s:
bhuktvehasakalānbhogānante viṣṇupadaṃ vrajet /
kṣetradhānyasuvarṇānāṃ ppāptaye dhāraṇīṃ smaret //
1.70.d:
भुक्त्वेहसकलान्भोगानन्ते विष्णुपदं व्रजेत् ।
क्षेत्रधान्यसुवर्णानां प्पाप्तये धारणीं स्मरेत् ॥
1.70.m: having enjoyed all pleasures here, goes to the abode of Viṣṇu at the end. / To obtain lands, grains, and gold, one should remember the Earth-goddess,

1.70.s:
devīṃ dūrvādalaśyāmāṃ dadhānāṃ śālimañjarīm /
cintayedbhāratīṃ devīṃ vīṇāpustakadhāriṇīm //
1.70.d:
देवीं दूर्वादलश्यामां दधानां शालिमञ्जरीम् ।
चिन्तयेद्भारतीं देवीं वीणापुस्तकधारिणीम् ॥
1.70.m: the goddess dark as a blade of dūrvā grass, holding a stalk of winter rice. / One should contemplate the goddess Bhāratī holding a vīṇā and a book,

1.70.s:
dakṣiṇe devadevasya pūrṇacandranibhānanām /
kṣīrābdhiphenapuñjābhe vasānāṃ śvetavāsasī //
1.70.d:
दक्षिणे देवदेवस्य पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम् ।
क्षीराब्धिफेनपुञ्जाभे वसानां श्वेतवाससी ॥
1.70.m: to the right of the God of gods, her face resembling the full moon, / dressed in two white garments resembling a mass of foam from the ocean of milk.

1.70.s:
bhāratyā sahitaṃ yo vai dhyāyeddvevaṃ parātparam /
vedavedārthatattvajño jāyate sarvavittamaḥ //
1.70.d:
भारत्या सहितं यो वै ध्यायेद्द्वेवं परात्परम् ।
वेदवेदार्थतत्त्वज्ञो जायते सर्ववित्तमः ॥
1.70.m: Whoever meditates on the God higher than the highest together with Bhāratī / becomes one who knows the truth of the Vedas and their meaning, the foremost knower of all.

1.70.s:
nārasiṃhamivātmānaṃ devaṃ dhyātvātibhairavam /
śaśtraṃ saṃmantrya mantreṇa śabrūnhatvā nivartate //
1.70.d:
नारसिंहमिवात्मानं देवं ध्यात्वातिभैरवम् ।
शश्त्रं संमन्त्र्य मन्त्रेण शब्रून्हत्वा निवर्तते ॥
1.70.m: Meditating on oneself as Nṛsiṃha, the exceedingly terrible deity, / having consecrated a weapon with the mantra and slain one's enemies, one returns.

1.70.s:
nārasiṃhena bījena mantraṃ saṃyojya sādhakaḥ /
śatamaṣṭottaraṃ jaṇtvā vāmahastābhimantritāḥ //
1.70.d:
नारसिंहेन बीजेन मन्त्रं संयोज्य साधकः ।
शतमष्टोत्तरं जण्त्वा वामहस्ताभिमन्त्रिताः ॥
1.70.m: Combining the mantra with the seed-syllable of Nṛsiṃha, the practitioner, / having recited it one hundred and eight times, with [waters] consecrated with the left hand,

1.70.s:
punaḥ punarapaḥ siṃcetsarpadaṣṭo 'pi jīvati /
gāruḍena ca saṃyojya pañcārṇena japettadā //
1.70.d:
पुनः पुनरपः सिंचेत्सर्पदष्टो ऽपि जीवति ।
गारुडेन च संयोज्य पञ्चार्णेन जपेत्तदा ॥
1.70.m: should sprinkle waters again and again; even one bitten by a snake survives. / Combining it with the five-syllabled Garuḍa [mantra], one should then recite it.

1.70.s:
nirviṣīkaraṇe dhyāyedviṣṇuṃ garuḍavāhanam /
aśokaphalake tārkṣyamālikhyāśokasaṃhatau //
1.70.d:
निर्विषीकरणे ध्यायेद्विष्णुं गरुडवाहनम् ।
अशोकफलके तार्क्ष्यमालिख्याशोकसंहतौ ॥
1.70.m: For neutralizing poison, one should meditate on Viṣṇu mounted upon Garuḍa. / Having drawn Garuḍa on an aśoka-wood tablet amidst a grove of aśoka trees,

1.70.s:
aśokapuṣpaiḥ saṃpūjya bhagavantaṃ tadagrataḥ /
juhuyāttāni puṣpāṇi trisaṃdhyaṃ saptapatrakam //
1.70.d:
अशोकपुष्पैः संपूज्य भगवन्तं तदग्रतः ।
जुहुयात्तानि पुष्पाणि त्रिसंध्यं सप्तपत्रकम् ॥
1.70.m: having worshipped the Lord with aśoka flowers in front of it, / one should offer those flowers at the three twilights [along with] a seven-leafed [sprig].

1.70.s:
pratyakṣo jāyate pakṣī varamiṣṭaṃ prayacchati /
gāṇapatyena saṃyojya japellakṣaṃ payovrataḥ //
1.70.d:
प्रत्यक्षो जायते पक्षी वरमिष्टं प्रयच्छति ।
गाणपत्येन संयोज्य जपेल्लक्षं पयोव्रतः ॥
1.70.m: The bird becomes visible before one's eyes and grants the desired boon. / Combining it with the Gāṇapatya [mantra], living on milk, one should recite one hundred thousand times.

1.70.s:
mahāgaṇapatiṃ devaṃ pratyakṣamiha paśyati /
vāṇibījena saṃyuktaṃ ṣaṇmāsaṃ yojayennaraḥ //
1.70.d:
महागणपतिं देवं प्रत्यक्षमिह पश्यति ।
वाणिबीजेन संयुक्तं षण्मासं योजयेन्नरः ॥
1.70.m: Here one sees the god Mahāgaṇapati visibly present before one's eyes. / A man should employ it joined with the seed-syllable of Speech for six months;

1.70.s:
mahākavivaro bhūtvā mohayetsakalaṃ jagat /
hutvā guṅcīśakalānyarddhāgulamitāni ca //
1.70.d:
महाकविवरो भूत्वा मोहयेत्सकलं जगत् ।
हुत्वा गुङ्चीशकलान्यर्द्धागुलमितानि च ॥
1.70.m: becoming a foremost great poet, he can enchant the entire world. / Having offered pieces of guñjā measured to half an aṅgula,

1.70.s:
dadhimadhvājyayuktāni mṛtyuṃ jayati sādhakaḥ /
śanaiśvara dine samyak spṛṣṭvā śvatthaṃ ca pāṇinā //
1.70.d:
दधिमध्वाज्ययुक्तानि मृत्युं जयति साधकः ।
शनैश्वर दिने सम्यक् स्पृष्ट्वा श्वत्थं च पाणिना ॥
1.70.m: combined with curd, honey, and clarified butter, the practitioner conquers death. / On a Saturday, properly touching an aśvattha tree with the hand,

1.70.s:
japtvā cāṣṭaśataṃ yuddhe hyapamṛtyuṃ jayatyasau /
pañcaviṃśatidhā japtvā nityaṃ prātaḥ pibejjalam //
1.70.d:
जप्त्वा चाष्टशतं युद्धे ह्यपमृत्युं जयत्यसौ ।
पञ्चविंशतिधा जप्त्वा नित्यं प्रातः पिबेज्जलम् ॥
1.70.m: and having recited it one hundred and eight times, he conquers untimely death in battle. / Having recited it twenty-five times, he should drink water every morning;

1.70.s:
sarvapāpavinirmukto jñānavān rogavarjitaḥ /
kuṃbhaṃ saṃsthāpya vidhivadāpūrya śuddhavāriṇā //
1.70.d:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो ज्ञानवान् रोगवर्जितः ।
कुंभं संस्थाप्य विधिवदापूर्य शुद्धवारिणा ॥
1.70.m: freed from all sins, he becomes wise and devoid of diseases. / Setting up a pot according to rule and filling it with pure water,

1.70.s:
japtvāyutaṃ tatastenābhiṣekaḥ sarvaroganut /
candrasūryoparāge tu hyupoṣyāṣṭasahasrakam //
1.70.d:
जप्त्वायुतं ततस्तेनाभिषेकः सर्वरोगनुत् ।
चन्द्रसूर्योपरागे तु ह्युपोष्याष्टसहस्रकम् ॥
1.70.m: having recited it ten thousand times, a bath with that removes all illnesses. / During an eclipse of the moon or the sun, having fasted, [reciting] eight thousand times,

1.70.s:
spṛṣṭvā brāhmīdhṛtaṃ japtvā pibetsādhakasattamaḥ /
medhāṃ kavitvaṃ vāksiddhiṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.70.d:
स्पृष्ट्वा ब्राह्मीधृतं जप्त्वा पिबेत्साधकसत्तमः ।
मेधां कवित्वं वाक्सिद्धिं लभते नात्र संशयः ॥
1.70.m: touching brāhmī-ghee and reciting, the best of practitioners should drink it; / he gains intelligence, poetic skill, and the power of speech; there is no doubt in this.

1.70.s:
juhuyādayutaṃ vilvairmahādhanapatirbhavet /
nārāyaṇasya mantro 'yaṃ sarvamantrottamottamaḥ //
1.70.d:
जुहुयादयुतं विल्वैर्महाधनपतिर्भवेत् ।
नारायणस्य मन्त्रो ऽयं सर्वमन्त्रोत्तमोत्तमः ॥
1.70.m: One should offer ten thousand [oblations] with bilva fruits; one becomes a lord of great wealth. / This mantra of Nārāyaṇa is the most supreme of all mantras,

1.70.s:
ālayaḥ sarvasiddhīnāṃ kathitastava nārada /
nārāyaṇāya śabdānte vidmahe padamīrayet //
1.70.d:
आलयः सर्वसिद्धीनां कथितस्तव नारद ।
नारायणाय शब्दान्ते विद्महे पदमीरयेत् ॥
1.70.m: the abode of all perfections, spoken unto you, O Nārada. / After the word 'nārāyaṇāya', one should utter the word 'vidmahe';

1.70.s:
vāsudevapadaṃ ṅeṃtaṃ dhīmahīti tato vadet /
tanno viṣṇuḥ pracovarṇānsaṃvadeñcodayāditi //
1.70.d:
वासुदेवपदं ङेंतं धीमहीति ततो वदेत् ।
तन्नो विष्णुः प्रचोवर्णान्संवदेञ्चोदयादिति ॥
1.70.m: then one should say the word 'vāsudeva' in the dative case, and 'dhīmahi'; / then 'tanno viṣṇuḥ pracodavārṇān' and say 'pracodayāt'.

1.70.s:
eṣoktā viṣṇugāyatrī sarvapāpapraṇāśinī /
tāro hṛdbhagavān ṅeṃto vāsudevāya kīrtitaḥ //
1.70.d:
एषोक्ता विष्णुगायत्री सर्वपापप्रणाशिनी ।
तारो हृद्भगवान् ङेंतो वासुदेवाय कीर्तितः ॥
1.70.m: This is declared as the Viṣṇugāyatrī, the destroyer of all sins. / Oṃ, namaḥ, bhagavate in the dative case, and vāsudevāya are stated:

1.70.s:
dvādaśārṇo mahāmantro bhuktimuktipradāyakaḥ /
strīśūdrāṇāṃ vitāro 'yaṃ satārastu dvijanmanām //
1.70.d:
द्वादशार्णो महामन्त्रो भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायकः ।
स्त्रीशूद्राणां वितारो ऽयं सतारस्तु द्विजन्मनाम् ॥
1.70.m: this twelve-syllabled great mantra bestows enjoyment and liberation. / For women and Śūdras it is without Oṃ, but for the twice-born it is with Oṃ.

1.70.s:
prajāpatirmuniścāsya gāyatrī chanda īritaḥ /
devatā vāsudevastu bījaṃ śaktirdhruvaśca hṛt //
1.70.d:
प्रजापतिर्मुनिश्चास्य गायत्री छन्द ईरितः ।
देवता वासुदेवस्तु बीजं शक्तिर्ध्रुवश्च हृत् ॥
1.70.m: Prajāpati is its seer, the metre is said to be Gāyatrī, / the deity is Vāsudeva, the seed-syllable is [Oṃ], the śakti is [namaḥ].

1.70.s:
candrākṣivedapañcarṇaiḥ samastenāṅgakalpanam /
mūrdhni bhāle dṛśorāsye gale dorhṛdaye punaḥ //
1.70.d:
चन्द्राक्षिवेदपञ्चर्णैः समस्तेनाङ्गकल्पनम् ।
मूर्ध्नि भाले दृशोरास्ये गले दोर्हृदये पुनः ॥
1.70.m: The assignment of the limbs is done with one, two, four, five syllables, and all together. / On the crown of the head, forehead, eyes, face, throat, arms, and heart,

1.70.s:
kukṣau nābhau dhvaje jānudvaye pādadvaye tathā /
nyāsetkramān mantravarṇānsṛṣṭinyāso 'yamīritaḥ //
1.70.d:
कुक्षौ नाभौ ध्वजे जानुद्वये पादद्वये तथा ।
न्यासेत्क्रमान् मन्त्रवर्णान्सृष्टिन्यासो ऽयमीरितः ॥
1.70.m: on the belly, navel, generative organ, the two knees, and likewise the two feet, / one should place the syllables of the mantra in order; this is declared as the nyāsa of creation.

1.70.s:
hṛdādimastakāntaṃ tu sthitinyāsaṃ pracakṣate /
pādādārabhya mūrddhānaṃ nyāsaṃ saṃhārakaṃ viduḥ //
1.70.d:
हृदादिमस्तकान्तं तु स्थितिन्यासं प्रचक्षते ।
पादादारभ्य मूर्द्धानं न्यासं संहारकं विदुः ॥
1.70.m: From the heart to the head is spoken of as the nyāsa of preservation. / Beginning from the feet up to the head, they know as the nyāsa of dissolution.

1.70.s:
tattvanyāsaṃ tataḥ kuryātsarvatantreṣu gopitam /
bīvaṃ prāṇaṃ tathā cittaṃ hṛtpadmaṃ sūryamaṇḍalam //
1.70.d:
तत्त्वन्यासं ततः कुर्यात्सर्वतन्त्रेषु गोपितम् ।
बीवं प्राणं तथा चित्तं हृत्पद्मं सूर्यमण्डलम् ॥
1.70.m: Then one should perform the nyāsa of tattvas concealed in all tantras: / the soul, the vital breath, and the mind, the heart-lotus, the orb of the sun,

1.70.s:
candrāgnimaṇḍale caiva vāsudevaṃ tataḥ param /
saṃkarṣaṇaṃ ca pradyumnamaniruddhaṃ tataḥ param //
1.70.d:
चन्द्राग्निमण्डले चैव वासुदेवं ततः परम् ।
संकर्षणं च प्रद्युम्नमनिरुद्धं ततः परम् ॥
1.70.m: the orb of the moon and the fire, and beyond that, Vāsudeva, / Saṃkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, and beyond that, Aniruddha,

1.70.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ cakramatastattvāni dvādaśaiva tu /
mūlārṇahṛtparāyādyamātmane hṛdayāntimam //
1.70.d:
नारायणं चक्रमतस्तत्त्वानि द्वादशैव तु ।
मूलार्णहृत्परायाद्यमात्मने हृदयान्तिमम् ॥
1.70.m: Nārāyaṇa, and the discus: these are indeed the twelve tattvas. / Beginning with each root syllable, followed by namaḥ, followed by ātmane, ending with namaḥ,

1.70.s:
tattve nāma samuñcaryya nyasenmūrddhādiṣu kramāt /
pūrvoktaṃ dhyānamatrāpi bhānulakṣajapo manoḥ //
1.70.d:
तत्त्वे नाम समुञ्चर्य्य न्यसेन्मूर्द्धादिषु क्रमात् ।
पूर्वोक्तं ध्यानमत्रापि भानुलक्षजपो मनोः ॥
1.70.m: pronouncing the name of each tattva, one should place them on the head and other parts in order. / Here too the meditation is as previously stated; the recitation of the mantra is twelve hundred thousand times.

1.70.s:
tadṛśāṃśaṃ tilairājyalolitairhavanaṃ caret /
pīṭhe pūrvodite mantrī mūrti saṃkalpya mūlataḥ //
1.70.d:
तदृशांशं तिलैराज्यलोलितैर्हवनं चरेत् ।
पीठे पूर्वोदिते मन्त्री मूर्ति संकल्प्य मूलतः ॥
1.70.m: One should perform homa with a tenth part of that using sesame seeds mixed with ghee. / On the previously stated ritual seat, the mantrin, projecting the form by means of the root mantra,

1.70.s:
tasyāmāvāhya deveśaṃ vāsudevaṃ prapūjayet /
aṅgāni pūrvamabhyarcya vāsudevādikāstataḥ //
1.70.d:
तस्यामावाह्य देवेशं वासुदेवं प्रपूजयेत् ।
अङ्गानि पूर्वमभ्यर्च्य वासुदेवादिकास्ततः ॥
1.70.m: having invoked the Lord of gods into it, should worship Vāsudeva. / Having first worshipped the limbs, then Vāsudeva and the others,

1.70.s:
śāntyādiśaktayaḥ pūjyāḥ prāgvaddikṣu vidikṣu ca /
tṛtīyāvaraṇe pūjyāḥ proktā dvādaśa mūrtayaḥ //
1.70.d:
शान्त्यादिशक्तयः पूज्याः प्राग्वद्दिक्षु विदिक्षु च ।
तृतीयावरणे पूज्याः प्रोक्ता द्वादश मूर्तयः ॥
1.70.m: the powers such as Śānti are to be worshipped in the directions and intermediate directions as before; / in the third enclosure, the twelve forms that have been declared are to be worshipped.

1.70.s:
indrādyānāyudhairyuktān pūjayeddharaṇīgṛhe /
evamāvaraṇairiṣṭvā pañcabhirviṣṇumavyayam //
1.70.d:
इन्द्राद्यानायुधैर्युक्तान् पूजयेद्धरणीगृहे ।
एवमावरणैरिष्ट्वा पञ्चभिर्विष्णुमव्ययम् ॥
1.70.m: One should worship Indra and the others equipped with their weapons in the earth-abode. / Thus, having worshipped the imperishable Viṣṇu with five enclosures,

1.70.s:
prāpnuyātsakalānarthānante viṣṇupade vrajet /
puruṣottamasaṃjñasya viṣṇorbhedacatuṣṭayam //
1.70.d:
प्राप्नुयात्सकलानर्थानन्ते विष्णुपदे व्रजेत् ।
पुरुषोत्तमसंज्ञस्य विष्णोर्भेदचतुष्टयम् ॥
1.70.m: one obtains all desires and goes to the abode of Viṣṇu at the end. / Of Viṣṇu named Puruṣottama, there is a fourfold division.

1.70.s:
trailokyamohanasteṣāṃ prathamaḥ parikīrtitaḥ /
śrīkaraśca hṛṣīkeśaḥ kṛṣaaṇaścātra caturthakaḥ //
1.70.d:
त्रैलोक्यमोहनस्तेषां प्रथमः परिकीर्तितः ।
श्रीकरश्च हृषीकेशः कृषअणश्चात्र चतुर्थकः ॥
1.70.m: Among them, Trailokyamohana is proclaimed as the first; / Śrīkara, Hṛṣīkeśa, and Kṛṣṇa is the fourth here.

1.70.s:
tāraḥ kāmo ramā paścān ṅeṃtaḥ syātpuruṣottamaḥ /
varmāstrāṇyagnipriyānto mantro vahnīnduvarṇavān //
1.70.d:
तारः कामो रमा पश्चान् ङेंतः स्यात्पुरुषोत्तमः ।
वर्मास्त्राण्यग्निप्रियान्तो मन्त्रो वह्नीन्दुवर्णवान् ॥
1.70.m: Oṃ, klīm, śrīm, and then puruṣottama in the dative case, / followed by hum phaṭ svāhā; the mantra consists of thirty-one syllables.

1.70.s:
brahmā muniḥ syādgāyatrī chandaḥ prokto 'tha devatā /
puruṣottamasaṃjño 'tra bījaśaktīsmarandire //
1.70.d:
ब्रह्मा मुनिः स्याद्गायत्री छन्दः प्रोक्तो ऽथ देवता ।
पुरुषोत्तमसंज्ञो ऽत्र बीजशक्तीस्मरन्दिरे ॥
1.70.m: Brahmā is the seer, Gāyatrī is declared as the metre, and the deity / is named Puruṣottama; the seed-syllable and śakti are Kāma and Ramā.

1.70.s:
bhūcandraikarasākṣyakṣimantravarṇorvibhāgataḥ /
kṛtvāṅgāni tato dhyāyedvidhivatpuruṣottamam //
1.70.d:
भूचन्द्रैकरसाक्ष्यक्षिमन्त्रवर्णोर्विभागतः ।
कृत्वाङ्गानि ततो ध्यायेद्विधिवत्पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
1.70.m: Dividing the syllables of the mantra by one, one, one, six, two, and two, / having assigned the limbs, one should then properly meditate on Puruṣottama:

1.70.s:
samudyadādityanibhaṃ śaṅkhacakragadāṃbujaiḥ /
lasatkaraṃ pītavasraṃ smarecchrīpuruṣottamam //
1.70.d:
समुद्यदादित्यनिभं शङ्खचक्रगदांबुजैः ।
लसत्करं पीतवस्रं स्मरेच्छ्रीपुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
1.70.m: Resembling the rising sun, with hands shining with conch, discus, mace, and lotus, / dressed in yellow garments—one should remember the glorious Puruṣottama,

1.70.s:
mahāratnaughakhacitasphurattoraṇamaṇḍape /
mauktikaughaśamadamavirājitavitānake //
1.70.d:
महारत्नौघखचितस्फुरत्तोरणमण्डपे ।
मौक्तिकौघशमदमविराजितवितानके ॥
1.70.m: in a pavilion with glittering arched doorways studded with masses of great gems, / with a canopy adorned with clusters of pearls of calm brilliance,

1.70.s:
nṛtyaddevāṅganāvṛndakvaṇātkiṅkiṇinūpure /
lasanmāṇikyavedyāṃ tu dītpārkāyutatejasi //
1.70.d:
नृत्यद्देवाङ्गनावृन्दक्वणात्किङ्किणिनूपुरे ।
लसन्माणिक्यवेद्यां तु दीत्पार्कायुततेजसि ॥
1.70.m: where anklets and tiny bells tinkle on host of celestial maidens dancing, / on a platform of shining rubies possessing the radiance of ten thousand blazing suns,

1.70.s:
vṛndārakavrātakirīṭāgraratnābhicarcite /
navalakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ juhuyāttaddaśāṃśataḥ //
1.70.d:
वृन्दारकव्रातकिरीटाग्ररत्नाभिचर्चिते ।
नवलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं जुहुयात्तद्दशांशतः ॥
1.70.m: anointed with the luster of jewels on the crests of crowns of hosts of gods. / One should recite the mantra nine hundred thousand times and offer oblation with a tenth of that.

1.70.s:
utphullaiḥ kamalaiḥ pīṭhe pūrvokte vaiṣṇaver'cayet /
evamārādhya deveśaṃ prāpnoti mahatīṃ śriyam //
1.70.d:
उत्फुल्लैः कमलैः पीठे पूर्वोक्ते वैष्णवेर्ऽचयेत् ।
एवमाराध्य देवेशं प्राप्नोति महतीं श्रियम् ॥
1.70.m: One should worship with fully blossomed lotuses on the previously stated Vaiṣṇava ritual seat. / Having thus worshipped the Lord of gods, one obtains great prosperity;

1.70.s:
putrānpautrānyaśaḥ kāntiṃ bhuktiṃ muktiṃ ca vindati /
uttiṣṭeti padaṃ paścācchrīkarāgnipriyāntimaḥ //
1.70.d:
पुत्रान्पौत्रान्यशः कान्तिं भुक्तिं मुक्तिं च विन्दति ।
उत्तिष्टेति पदं पश्चाच्छ्रीकराग्निप्रियान्तिमः ॥
1.70.m: he obtains sons, grandsons, fame, radiance, enjoyment, and liberation. / The word 'uttiṣṭha', followed by 'śrīkara', and ending with 'svāhā'—

1.70.s:
aṣṭārṇo 'sya munirvyāsaḥ paṅktiśchanda udāhṛtam /
śrīkārākhyo hariḥ prokto devatā sakaleṣṭadaḥ //
1.70.d:
अष्टार्णो ऽस्य मुनिर्व्यासः पङ्क्तिश्छन्द उदाहृतम् ।
श्रीकाराख्यो हरिः प्रोक्तो देवता सकलेष्टदः ॥
1.70.m: this is eight-syllabled; its seer is Vyāsa, the metre is said to be Paṅkti, / the deity is Hari named Śrīkara, the bestower of all desires.

1.70.s:
bhīṣayadvitayaṃ hṛtsyāt trāsayadvitayaṃ śiraḥ /
śikhā pramarddayadvandvaṃ varma pradhvaṃsayadvayam //
1.70.d:
भीषयद्वितयं हृत्स्यात् त्रासयद्वितयं शिरः ।
शिखा प्रमर्द्दयद्वन्द्वं वर्म प्रध्वंसयद्वयम् ॥
1.70.m: The two [words] *bhīṣaya bhīṣaya* are the heart; the two [words] *trāsaya trāsaya* are the head; / the pair *pramardaya pramardaya* is the crest; the two [words] *pradhvaṃsaya pradhvaṃsaya* are the armor;

1.70.s:
asraṃ rakṣadvayaṃ sarve humantāḥ samudīritāḥ /
mastake netrayoḥ kaṇṭhahṛdaye nābhideśake //
1.70.d:
अस्रं रक्षद्वयं सर्वे हुमन्ताः समुदीरिताः ।
मस्तके नेत्रयोः कण्ठहृदये नाभिदेशके ॥
1.70.m: the two [words] *rakṣa rakṣa* are the weapon; all are declared to end in *hum*. / On the head, on the two eyes, on the throat, on the heart, in the region of the navel,

1.70.s:
ūrūjaṅghāṃyugmeṣu mantravarṇānkramānnyataset /
tataḥ puruṣasūktoktamantrairnyāsaṃ samācaret //
1.70.d:
ऊरूजङ्घांयुग्मेषु मन्त्रवर्णान्क्रमान्न्यतसेत् ।
ततः पुरुषसूक्तोक्तमन्त्रैर्न्यासं समाचरेत् ॥
1.70.m: and on the pairs of thighs and shanks, one should perform the ritual placement of the syllables of the mantra in order. / Then one should perform the ritual placement with the mantras spoken in the Puruṣasūkta:

1.70.s:
mukhe nyasedbrāhmaṇo 'sya mukhamāsīdimaṃ manum /
bāhuyugme tathā bāhūṃrājanya iti vinyaset //
1.70.d:
मुखे न्यसेद्ब्राह्मणो ऽस्य मुखमासीदिमं मनुम् ।
बाहुयुग्मे तथा बाहूंराजन्य इति विन्यसेत् ॥
1.70.m: On the mouth one should place the mantra *brāhmaṇo 'sya mukham āsīt*; / likewise on the pair of arms one should place *bāhū rājanyaḥ*;

1.70.s:
ūrū tadasya yadvaiśya imamūrudvaye nyaset /
nyasetpādadvaye mantrī padbhyāṃ śūdro ajāyata //
1.70.d:
ऊरू तदस्य यद्वैश्य इममूरुद्वये न्यसेत् ।
न्यसेत्पादद्वये मन्त्री पद्भ्यां शूद्रो अजायत ॥
1.70.m: one should place this *ūrū tad asya yad vaiśyaḥ* on the pair of thighs; / the practitioner should place on the pair of feet *padbhyāṃ śūdro ajāyata*.

1.70.s:
cakraṃ śaṅkhaṃ gadāṃ padmaṃ karāgreṣvatha vinyaset /
evaṃ nyāsavidhiṃ kṛtvā dhyāyetpūrvoktamaṇḍape //
1.70.d:
चक्रं शङ्खं गदां पद्मं कराग्रेष्वथ विन्यसेत् ।
एवं न्यासविधिं कृत्वा ध्यायेत्पूर्वोक्तमण्डपे ॥
1.70.m: Then one should place the discus, the conch, the mace, and the lotus on the fingertips. / Having thus performed the rite of ritual placement, one should meditate in the previously described pavilion:

1.70.s:
aruṇābjāsanasthasya tārkṣyasyopari saṃsthitam /
pūrvoktarūpiṇaṃ devaṃ śrīkaraṃ lokamohanam //
1.70.d:
अरुणाब्जासनस्थस्य तार्क्ष्यस्योपरि संस्थितम् ।
पूर्वोक्तरूपिणं देवं श्रीकरं लोकमोहनम् ॥
1.70.m: upon Garuḍa seated on a red lotus seat, / the god who has the previously stated form, the granter of prosperity, who enchants the world.

1.70.s:
dhyātvaivaṃ pūjayedaṣṭalakṣaṃ mantrī daśāṃśataḥ /
raktāṃbujaiḥ samidbhiśca vilvakṣīridrumodbhavaiḥ //
1.70.d:
ध्यात्वैवं पूजयेदष्टलक्षं मन्त्री दशांशतः ।
रक्तांबुजैः समिद्भिश्च विल्वक्षीरिद्रुमोद्भवैः ॥
1.70.m: Having thus meditated, the practitioner should recite eight hundred thousand times, and one-tenth of that / [he should offer] in fire oblations with red lotuses, kindling sticks from bilva and milky-sapped trees,

1.70.s:
payo 'nnaiḥ sarpiṣā hutvā pratyekaṃ susamāhitaḥ /
aśvatthoduṃbaraplakṣavaṭāḥ kṣīridrumāḥ smṛtā //
1.70.d:
पयो ऽन्नैः सर्पिषा हुत्वा प्रत्येकं सुसमाहितः ।
अश्वत्थोदुंबरप्लक्षवटाः क्षीरिद्रुमाः स्मृता ॥
1.70.m: milk-rice, and clarified butter, one by one, with concentrated mind. / The aśvattha, uḍumbara, plakṣa, and banyan are remembered as milky-sapped trees.

1.70.s:
pūjayedvaiṣṇave pīṭhe mūrtiṃ saṃkalpya mūlataḥ /
aṅgāvaraṇadikpālahetibhiḥ sahitaṃ vibhum //
1.70.d:
पूजयेद्वैष्णवे पीठे मूर्तिं संकल्प्य मूलतः ।
अङ्गावरणदिक्पालहेतिभिः सहितं विभुम् ॥
1.70.m: One should worship the all-pervading Lord on a Vaiṣṇava ritual seat, envisioning His form by means of the root-mantra, / accompanied by the limbs, the retinue, the guardians of the directions, and the weapons.

1.70.s:
itthaṃ siddhe manau matrī prayogānpūrvavañcaret /
tāro hṛdbhagavān ṅeṃto varāheti tataḥ param //
1.70.d:
इत्थं सिद्धे मनौ मत्री प्रयोगान्पूर्ववञ्चरेत् ।
तारो हृद्भगवान् ङेंतो वराहेति ततः परम् ॥
1.70.m: When the mantra is thus mastered, the practitioner should perform the rites as before. / [The mantra begins with] the Praṇava, [followed by] *hṛt* [namaḥ], *bhagavān* ending in the dative, and then *varāha*;

1.70.s:
rūpāya bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ syāllohitakāmikā ca ye /
bhūpatitvaṃ ca me dehi dadāpaya śucipriyā //
1.70.d:
रूपाय भूर्भुवः स्वः स्याल्लोहितकामिका च ये ।
भूपतित्वं च मे देहि ददापय शुचिप्रिया ॥
1.70.m: *rūpāya*, [then] *bhūḥ bhuvaḥ svaḥ*, *lohitakāmikāye*, / and *bhūpatitvaṃ ca me dehi dadāpaya*, ending with the beloved of Agni [*svāhā*].

1.70.s:
rāmāgnivarṇo mantro 'yaṃ bhārgavo 'sya munirmataḥ /
chando 'nuṣṭubdevatādivarāhaḥ samudīritaḥ //
1.70.d:
रामाग्निवर्णो मन्त्रो ऽयं भार्गवो ऽस्य मुनिर्मतः ।
छन्दो ऽनुष्टुब्देवतादिवराहः समुदीरितः ॥
1.70.m: This mantra has thirty-three syllables; its sage is considered to be Bhārgava; / the meter is anuṣṭubh, and the deity is proclaimed to be Ādivarāha.

1.70.s:
ekadaṃṣṭrāya hṛdayaṃ vyomolkāyaga śiraḥ smṛtam /
śikhā tejo 'dhipataye viśvarūpāya varma ca //
1.70.d:
एकदंष्ट्राय हृदयं व्योमोल्कायग शिरः स्मृतम् ।
शिखा तेजो ऽधिपतये विश्वरूपाय वर्म च ॥
1.70.m: To Ekadaṃṣṭra is the heart; *vyomolkāya* is remembered as the head; / the crest is to Tejodhipati; the armor is to Viśvarūpa;

1.70.s:
mahādaṃṣṭrāya cāstraṃ syātpañcāṅgamiti kalpayet /
athavā giriṣaṭsaptabāṇairvasubhirakṣaraiḥ //
1.70.d:
महादंष्ट्राय चास्त्रं स्यात्पञ्चाङ्गमिति कल्पयेत् ।
अथवा गिरिषट्सप्तबाणैर्वसुभिरक्षरैः ॥
1.70.m: and the weapon is to Mahādaṃṣṭra; thus one should arrange the five limbs. / Or else, by means of seven, six, seven, five, and eight syllables,

1.70.s:
vibhaktairmantravaryasya pañcāgāṃni prakalpayet /
tatau dhyāyedanekārkanibhamādivarāhakam //
1.70.d:
विभक्तैर्मन्त्रवर्यस्य पञ्चागांनि प्रकल्पयेत् ।
ततौ ध्यायेदनेकार्कनिभमादिवराहकम् ॥
1.70.m: divided from the excellent mantra, one should form the five limbs. / Then one should meditate on the Primeval Varāha, radiant like many suns,

1.70.s:
āṃ hrīṃ svarṇanibhaṃ jānvoradho nābheḥ sitaprabham /
iṣṭābhītigadāśaṅkhacakraśaktyasikheṭakān //
1.70.d:
आं ह्रीं स्वर्णनिभं जान्वोरधो नाभेः सितप्रभम् ।
इष्टाभीतिगदाशङ्खचक्रशक्त्यसिखेटकान् ॥
1.70.m: [with the seed-syllables] *āṃ hrīṃ*, resembling gold below the knees, and possessing a white radiance above the navel, / holding the boon, protection, mace, conch, discus, spear, sword, and shield

1.70.s:
dadhataṃ ca karairdaṃṣṭrāgralasaddharaṇiṃ smaret /
evaṃ dhyātvā japellakṣaṃ daśāṃśaṃ sarasīruhaiḥ //
1.70.d:
दधतं च करैर्दंष्ट्राग्रलसद्धरणिं स्मरेत् ।
एवं ध्यात्वा जपेल्लक्षं दशांशं सरसीरुहैः ॥
1.70.m: with His hands; and one should remember the earth shining on the tip of His tusk. / Having thus meditated, one should recite one hundred thousand times, and a tenth of that with lotuses

1.70.s:
madhvaktairjuhayātpīṭhe pūrvokte vaiṣṇave yajet /
mūlena mūrtiṃ saṅkalpya tasyāṃ sampūjayedvibhum //
1.70.d:
मध्वक्तैर्जुहयात्पीठे पूर्वोक्ते वैष्णवे यजेत् ।
मूलेन मूर्तिं सङ्कल्प्य तस्यां सम्पूजयेद्विभुम् ॥
1.70.m: smeared with honey one should offer in fire oblations; one should worship Him on the previously described Vaiṣṇava ritual seat. / Having conceived the form with the root-mantra, one should worship the all-pervading Lord in it,

1.70.s:
aṅgāvaraṇadikpālahetiyantraprasiddhaye /
japādevāvarni dadyāddhanaṃ dhānyaṃ mahīṃ śriyam //
1.70.d:
अङ्गावरणदिक्पालहेतियन्त्रप्रसिद्धये ।
जपादेवावर्नि दद्याद्धनं धान्यं महीं श्रियम् ॥
1.70.m: for the perfection of the limbs, retinue, guardians of the directions, weapons, and yantra. / From recitation alone, the earth will bestow wealth, grain, land, and prosperity.

1.70.s:
siṃhārke sitapakṣasyāṣṭamyāṃ gavyeṣu pañcasu /
śilāṃ śuddhāṃ vinikṣipya spṛṣṭvā tāmayutaṃ japet //
1.70.d:
सिंहार्के सितपक्षस्याष्टम्यां गव्येषु पञ्चसु ।
शिलां शुद्धां विनिक्षिप्य स्पृष्ट्वा तामयुतं जपेत् ॥
1.70.m: When the sun is in Leo, on the eighth day of the bright fortnight, placing a pure stone / into the five products of the cow, touching it, one should recite ten thousand times.

1.70.s:
udaṅmukhasvato mantrī tāṃ śilāṃ likhanedbhuvi /
bhūtapretāhicaurādikṛtāṃ bādhāṃ nivārayet //
1.70.d:
उदङ्मुखस्वतो मन्त्री तां शिलां लिखनेद्भुवि ।
भूतप्रेताहिचौरादिकृतां बाधां निवारयेत् ॥
1.70.m: The practitioner, facing north, should bury that stone in the ground; / he averts the affliction caused by spirits, ghosts, serpents, thieves, and the like.

1.70.s:
prātarbhṛgudine sādhyabhūtalānmṛdamāharet /
mantritāṃ mūlamantreṇa vibhajettāṃ tridhā punaḥ //
1.70.d:
प्रातर्भृगुदिने साध्यभूतलान्मृदमाहरेत् ।
मन्त्रितां मूलमन्त्रेण विभजेत्तां त्रिधा पुनः ॥
1.70.m: In the morning on a Friday, one should fetch clay from the ground to be mastered; / having consecrated it with the root-mantra, one should divide it again into three parts:

1.70.s:
cullyāmekaṃ samālipyāpyaparaṃ pākabhājane /
godugdhe paramāloḍya śodhitāṃstandulān kṣipet //
1.70.d:
चुल्ल्यामेकं समालिप्याप्यपरं पाकभाजने ।
गोदुग्धे परमालोड्य शोधितांस्तन्दुलान् क्षिपेत् ॥
1.70.m: smearing one [part] on the hearth, and the other on the cooking vessel, / having stirred [the third] in cow's milk, one should cast in cleansed grains of rice.

1.70.s:
samyak śuddhe śuciḥ keśe japanmantraṃ paceñcarum /
avatārya caruṃ paścādvahnau deyaṃ yathāvidhi //
1.70.d:
सम्यक् शुद्धे शुचिः केशे जपन्मन्त्रं पचेञ्चरुम् ।
अवतार्य चरुं पश्चाद्वह्नौ देयं यथाविधि ॥
1.70.m: Purified, in a thoroughly clean space, reciting the mantra, one should cook the sacrificial porridge. / Having taken down the sacrificial porridge, one should then offer it into the fire according to rule.

1.70.s:
sampūjya dhūpadīpādyaiḥ paścādājyaplutaṃ carum /
juhuyātsaṃskṛte vahnau aṣṭottaraśataṃ sudhīḥ //
1.70.d:
सम्पूज्य धूपदीपाद्यैः पश्चादाज्यप्लुतं चरुम् ।
जुहुयात्संस्कृते वह्नौ अष्टोत्तरशतं सुधीः ॥
1.70.m: Having worshiped with incense, lamps, and so forth, the wise practitioner should then offer into the consecrated fire / one hundred and eight times the sacrificial porridge drenched with clarified butter.

1.70.s:
evaṃ prajuhuyānmantrī kavivāreṣu saptasu /
virodho naśyati kṣetre śatrucaurādyupadravāḥ //
1.70.d:
एवं प्रजुहुयान्मन्त्री कविवारेषु सप्तसु ।
विरोधो नश्यति क्षेत्रे शत्रुचौराद्युपद्रवाः ॥
1.70.m: Thus the practitioner should offer in fire oblation on seven Fridays; / opposition in the field and troubles from enemies, thieves, and the like perish.

1.70.s:
bhānūdayepyāravāre sādhyakṣetrānmṛdaṃ punaḥ /
ādāya pūrvavidhinā havirāpādya pūrvavat //
1.70.d:
भानूदयेप्यारवारे साध्यक्षेत्रान्मृदं पुनः ।
आदाय पूर्वविधिना हविरापाद्य पूर्ववत् ॥
1.70.m: Also at sunrise on a Tuesday, taking clay again from the field to be mastered, / preparing the sacrificial offering according to the previous rule as before,

1.70.s:
juhuyādedhite vahnau pūrvasaṃkhyākamādarāt /
evaṃ sa saptāravāreṣu juhuyātkṣetrasiddhaye //
1.70.d:
जुहुयादेधिते वह्नौ पूर्वसंख्याकमादरात् ।
एवं स सप्तारवारेषु जुहुयात्क्षेत्रसिद्धये ॥
1.70.m: he should diligently offer into the kindled fire the previously stated number of times. / In this way he should offer fire oblations on seven Tuesdays for the mastery of the field.

1.70.s:
juhuyāllakṣasaṃkhyākaṃ gavyai ścaiva sapāyasaiḥ /
abhīṣṭabhūmyādhipatyaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.70.d:
जुहुयाल्लक्षसंख्याकं गव्यै श्चैव सपायसैः ।
अभीष्टभूम्याधिपत्यं लभते नात्र संशयः ॥
1.70.m: One should offer one hundred thousand fire oblations with the products of the cow and with milk-rice; / he attains lordship over the desired land; there is no doubt in this.

1.70.s:
udyaddoḥ paridhaṃ divyaṃ sitadaṃṣṭrāgrabhūdharam /
svarṇābhaṃ pārthive pīte maṇḍale susamāhitaḥ //
1.70.d:
उद्यद्दोः परिधं दिव्यं सितदंष्ट्राग्रभूधरम् ।
स्वर्णाभं पार्थिवे पीते मण्डले सुसमाहितः ॥
1.70.m: Having raised His arms like iron bars, divine, bearing the earth on the tip of His white tusk, / golden-hued, in the yellow earthly sacred diagram, with concentrated mind,

1.70.s:
dhyātvāpnoti mahīṃ ramyāṃ varāhasya prasādataḥ /
vāruṇe maṇḍale dhyāyedvārāhaṃ himasannibhagham //
1.70.d:
ध्यात्वाप्नोति महीं रम्यां वराहस्य प्रसादतः ।
वारुणे मण्डले ध्यायेद्वाराहं हिमसन्निभघम् ॥
1.70.m: having meditated, he obtains charming land through the grace of Varāha. / In the watery sacred diagram one should meditate on Varāha resembling snow;

1.70.s:
mahopadravaśāntiḥ syātsādhakasya na saṃśayaḥ /
vaśyārthaṃ ca sadā dhyāyedvarhyābhaṃ vahnimaṇḍe //
1.70.d:
महोपद्रवशान्तिः स्यात्साधकस्य न संशयः ।
वश्यार्थं च सदा ध्यायेद्वर्ह्याभं वह्निमण्डे ॥
1.70.m: there will be the pacification of great calamities for the practitioner, without doubt. / And for the sake of subjugation, one should always meditate on Him resembling fire in the fire sacred diagram;

1.70.s:
dhyāyedevaṃ ripūñcāṭe kṛṣṇābhaṃ vāyumaṇḍale /
hyamaṇḍalagataṃ svacchaṃ vārāhaṃ sarvasiddhidam //
1.70.d:
ध्यायेदेवं रिपूञ्चाटे कृष्णाभं वायुमण्डले ।
ह्यमण्डलगतं स्वच्छं वाराहं सर्वसिद्धिदम् ॥
1.70.m: one should thus meditate on Him as black-hued in the wind sacred diagram to drive away enemies. / In the ether sacred diagram, one should meditate on the pure Varāha, who bestows all perfections,

1.70.s:
śatrubhūtagrahakṣveḍāmayapīḍādiśāntaye /
bhagvardhīśayutaṃ vyomabindubhūṣitamastakam //
1.70.d:
शत्रुभूतग्रहक्ष्वेडामयपीडादिशान्तये ।
भग्वर्धीशयुतं व्योमबिन्दुभूषितमस्तकम् ॥
1.70.m: for the pacification of afflictions from enemies, spirits, astrological seizures, poison, illness, and the like. / [The syllable *h*], united with *ra*, *ī*, and the lord of wealth [long *ī*], the ether [*ha*] with its head adorned by the bindu—

1.70.s:
ekākṣaro varāhasya mantraḥ kalpadrumo 'paraḥ /
pūjādyārdhyādikaṃ sarvamasyāṃ pūrvoktavañcaret //
1.70.d:
एकाक्षरो वराहस्य मन्त्रः कल्पद्रुमो ऽपरः ।
पूजाद्यार्ध्यादिकं सर्वमस्यां पूर्वोक्तवञ्चरेत् ॥
1.70.m: this single-syllabled mantra of Varāha is another wish-granting tree. / One should perform all rites such as worship, offering of respectful water, and the like in this, as stated before.

1.70.s:
savāmakarṇānidrāsyādvarāhāya hṛdantimaḥ /
tārādyo vasuvarṇo 'yaṃ sarvaiśvaryapradāyakaḥ //
1.70.d:
सवामकर्णानिद्रास्याद्वराहाय हृदन्तिमः ।
ताराद्यो वसुवर्णो ऽयं सर्वैश्वर्यप्रदायकः ॥
1.70.m: [The syllable *g*] with the left ear [*u*], *nidrā* [*bha*] with *ra*, followed by *varāhāya*, ending with *hṛt* [*namaḥ*], / beginning with the Praṇava, this eight-syllabled [mantra] bestows all sovereign power.

1.70.s:
brahmā muniḥ syādgāyatrī chando vārāhasaṃjñakaḥ /
devaścandredvabdhinetraiḥ saveṇāṅgakriyā matā //
1.70.d:
ब्रह्मा मुनिः स्याद्गायत्री छन्दो वाराहसंज्ञकः ।
देवश्चन्द्रेद्वब्धिनेत्रैः सवेणाङ्गक्रिया मता ॥
1.70.m: Brahmā is the sage, the meter is gāyatrī, and the deity is named Varāha. / The ritual of the limbs is considered to be with one, two, four, and two syllables with *sva*.

1.70.s:
dhyānapūjāprayogādi prāgvadasyāpi kalpayet /
praṇavādau ca ṅentaṃ ca bhagavatīti padaṃ tataḥ /
dharaṇidvitayaṃ paścāddharerdvayamudīrayet //
1.70.d:
ध्यानपूजाप्रयोगादि प्राग्वदस्यापि कल्पयेत् ।
प्रणवादौ च ङेन्तं च भगवतीति पदं ततः ।
धरणिद्वितयं पश्चाद्धरेर्द्वयमुदीरयेत् ॥
1.70.m: One should perform meditation, worship, practical rites, and so forth for this as before. / Beginning with the Praṇava, and the word *bhagavatī* ending in the dative, / then two [words of] *dharaṇi*, and afterwards one should utter two [words of] *dhare*,

1.70.s:
ekonaviṃśatyarṇāḍhyo mantro vahnipriyāntimaḥ /
varāho 'sya muniśchando gāyatrī nivṛdādikā //
1.70.d:
एकोनविंशत्यर्णाढ्यो मन्त्रो वह्निप्रियान्तिमः ।
वराहो ऽस्य मुनिश्छन्दो गायत्री निवृदादिका ॥
1.70.m: and ending with the beloved of Agni [*svāhā*], is the mantra rich in nineteen syllables. / Varāha is its sage, the meter is gāyatrī, nivṛt, and so forth;

1.70.s:
devatā dharaṇī bījaṃ tāraḥśaktirvasupriyā /
rāmavedāgnibāṇākṣinetrārṇairaṅgarakalpanam //
1.70.d:
देवता धरणी बीजं तारःशक्तिर्वसुप्रिया ।
रामवेदाग्निबाणाक्षिनेत्रार्णैरङ्गरकल्पनम् ॥
1.70.m: the deity is Dharaṇī, the seed-syllable is the Praṇava, the power is the beloved of Vasu [*svāhā*]. / The arrangement of the limbs is with three, four, three, five, two, and two syllables.

1.70.s:
śyāmāṃ citravibhūṣāḍhyāṃ padmasthāṃ tuṅgasustanīm /
nīlāṃbujadvayaṃ śālimañjarīṃ ca śukraṃ karaiḥ //
1.70.d:
श्यामां चित्रविभूषाढ्यां पद्मस्थां तुङ्गसुस्तनीम् ।
नीलांबुजद्वयं शालिमञ्जरीं च शुक्रं करैः ॥
1.70.m: Dark-complexioned, adorned with diverse ornaments, standing on a lotus, having high, beautiful breasts, / holding two blue lotuses, a stalk of rice, and a parrot in Her hands,

1.70.s:
dadhatīṃ citravasanāṃ dharāṃ bhagavatīṃ smaret /
evaṃ dhyātvā japellakṣaṃ daśāṃśaṃ pāyasena tu //
1.70.d:
दधतीं चित्रवसनां धरां भगवतीं स्मरेत् ।
एवं ध्यात्वा जपेल्लक्षं दशांशं पायसेन तु ॥
1.70.m: wearing variegated garments—one should remember the divine Lady Earth. / Having thus meditated, one should recite one hundred thousand times, and offer a tenth of that with milk-rice

1.70.s:
sājyena juhuyānmantrī viṣṇoḥ pīṭhṭhe samarcayet /
mūrtiṃ saṃkalpya mūlena tasyāṃ vasumatīṃ yajet //
1.70.d:
साज्येन जुहुयान्मन्त्री विष्णोः पीठ्ठे समर्चयेत् ।
मूर्तिं संकल्प्य मूलेन तस्यां वसुमतीं यजेत् ॥
1.70.m: along with clarified butter; the practitioner should worship on the ritual seat of Viṣṇu. / Having conceived the form by the root-mantra, one should worship the Earth within it.

1.70.s:
aṅgāni pūrvamārādhya bhūvahnijalamārutān /
dikpātreṣu ca sampūjya koṇapatreṣu tatkalāḥ //
1.70.d:
अङ्गानि पूर्वमाराध्य भूवह्निजलमारुतान् ।
दिक्पात्रेषु च सम्पूज्य कोणपत्रेषु तत्कलाः ॥
1.70.m: Having first worshiped the limbs, one should worship the earth, fire, water, and wind / on the directional petals, and Her portions on the corner petals:

1.70.s:
nivṛttiśca pratiṣṭā ca vidyānāṃ taiśca tatkalāḥ /
indrādyānapi vañcādīnpūjayettadanantaram //
1.70.d:
निवृत्तिश्च प्रतिष्टा च विद्यानां तैश्च तत्कलाः ।
इन्द्राद्यानपि वञ्चादीन्पूजयेत्तदनन्तरम् ॥
1.70.m: Nivṛtti, Pratiṣṭhā, and Vidyā, and their kalās through them; / immediately after that, one should also worship Indra and the other [guardians of directions] and the thunderbolt and other weapons.

1.70.s:
evaṃ siddhe manau mantrī sādhayediṣṭamātmanaḥ /
dharaṇī prabhajannevaṃ paśuratnāṃbarādibhiḥ //
1.70.d:
एवं सिद्धे मनौ मन्त्री साधयेदिष्टमात्मनः ।
धरणी प्रभजन्नेवं पशुरत्नांबरादिभिः ॥
1.70.m: When the mantra is thus mastered, the practitioner achieves his desired aim, / worshiping Earth in this manner with cattle, jewels, garments, and the like.

1.70.s:
dharamyā vallabhaḥ sa syātsukhī jīvecchataṃ samā /
trailokyamohano mantro jagannāthasya kīrtyate //
1.70.d:
धरम्या वल्लभः स स्यात्सुखी जीवेच्छतं समा ।
त्रैलोक्यमोहनो मन्त्रो जगन्नाथस्य कीर्त्यते ॥
1.70.m:
He becomes dear to the earth and shall live happily for a hundred years.
Now the mantra of Jagannātha that bewilders the three worlds is proclaimed:

1.70.s:
tāraḥ kāmo ramā bījaṃ hṛdante puruṣottamaḥ /
śrīkaṇṭhaḥ pratirūpānte lakṣmīti ca nivāsi ca //
1.70.d:
तारः कामो रमा बीजं हृदन्ते पुरुषोत्तमः ।
श्रीकण्ठः प्रतिरूपान्ते लक्ष्मीति च निवासि च ॥
1.70.m:
The praṇava, the Kāma-bīja, Ramā's bīja, Puruṣottama following hṛt,
Śrīkaṇṭha followed by pratirūpa, and lakṣmī and nivāsi,

1.70.s:
sakalānte jagatpaścātkṣobhaṇeti padaṃ vadet /
sarvastrīhṛdayānte tu vidāraṇapadaṃ vadet //
1.70.d:
सकलान्ते जगत्पश्चात्क्षोभणेति पदं वदेत् ।
सर्वस्त्रीहृदयान्ते तु विदारणपदं वदेत् ॥
1.70.m:
after sakala one should utter the word jagat, then kṣobhaṇa;
after sarvastrīhṛdaya one should utter the word vidāraṇa;

1.70.s:
tatastribhuvanāntaṃ tu madonmādakareti ca /
surāsurānte manujasuṃdarījanavarṇataḥ //
1.70.d:
ततस्त्रिभुवनान्तं तु मदोन्मादकरेति च ।
सुरासुरान्ते मनुजसुंदरीजनवर्णतः ॥
1.70.m:
then following tribhuvana, madonmādakara;
after surāsura, through the syllables manujasundarījana,

1.70.s:
manāṃsi tāpayadvandvaṃ dīpayadvitayaṃ tataḥ /
śoṣayadvitayaṃ paścānmārayadvitayaṃ tataḥ //
1.70.d:
मनांसि तापयद्वन्द्वं दीपयद्वितयं ततः ।
शोषयद्वितयं पश्चान्मारयद्वितयं ततः ॥
1.70.m:
then manāṃsi, two tāpayas, then a pair of dīpayas,
then a pair of śoṣayas, then a pair of mārayas,

1.70.s:
staṃbhayadvitayaṃ bhūyo mohayadvitaya tataḥ /
drāvayadvitayaṃ tāvadākarṣayayugaṃ tataḥ //
dhyānapūjāprayogādi prāgvadasyāpi kalpayet /
praṇavādau ca ṅentaṃ ca bhagavatīti padaṃ tataḥ /
dharaṇidvitayaṃ paścāddharerdvayamudīrayet //
ekonaviṃśatyarṇāḍhyo mantro vahnipriyāntimaḥ /
varāho 'sya muniśchando gāyatrī nivṛdādikā //
devatā dharaṇī bījaṃ tāraḥśaktirvasupriyā /
rāmavedāgnibāṇākṣinevārṇairaṅgakalpanam //
śyāmāṃ citravibhūṣāḍhyāṃ padmasthāṃ tuṅgasustanīm /
nīlāṃbujadvayaṃ śālimañjarīñca śukaṃ karaiḥ //
dadhatīṃ citravasanāṃ dharāṃ bhagavatīṃ smaret /
evaṃ dhyātvā japellakṣaṃ daśāṃśaṃ pāyasena tu //
sājyena juhuyānmantrī viṣṇoḥ pīṭhe samarcayet /
mūrtiṃ saṃkalpya gūlena tasyāṃ vasumatīṃ yajet //
aṅgāni pūrvamārādhya bhūvahnijalamārutān /
dikpātreṣu ca sampūjya koṇapatreṣu tatkalāḥ //
1.70.d:
स्तंभयद्वितयं भूयो मोहयद्वितय ततः ।
द्रावयद्वितयं तावदाकर्षययुगं ततः ॥
ध्यानपूजाप्रयोगादि प्राग्वदस्यापि कल्पयेत् ।
प्रणवादौ च ङेन्तं च भगवतीति पदं ततः ।
धरणिद्वितयं पश्चाद्धरेर्द्वयमुदीरयेत् ॥
एकोनविंशत्यर्णाढ्यो मन्त्रो वह्निप्रियान्तिमः ।
वराहो ऽस्य मुनिश्छन्दो गायत्री निवृदादिका ॥
देवता धरणी बीजं तारःशक्तिर्वसुप्रिया ।
रामवेदाग्निबाणाक्षिनेवार्णैरङ्गकल्पनम् ॥
श्यामां चित्रविभूषाढ्यां पद्मस्थां तुङ्गसुस्तनीम् ।
नीलांबुजद्वयं शालिमञ्जरीञ्च शुकं करैः ॥
दधतीं चित्रवसनां धरां भगवतीं स्मरेत् ।
एवं ध्यात्वा जपेल्लक्षं दशांशं पायसेन तु ॥
साज्येन जुहुयान्मन्त्री विष्णोः पीठे समर्चयेत् ।
मूर्तिं संकल्प्य गूलेन तस्यां वसुमतीं यजेत् ॥
अङ्गानि पूर्वमाराध्य भूवह्निजलमारुतान् ।
दिक्पात्रेषु च सम्पूज्य कोणपत्रेषु तत्कलाः ॥
1.70.m:
again a pair of stambhayas, then a pair of mohayas,
then a pair of drāvayas, then a pair of ākarṣayas,

One should arrange the meditation, worship, ritual application, and the like for this also as before.
With the praṇava at the beginning, ending in the fourth case, then the word bhagavatī,
then two dharaṇīs, after that one should utter two haras;

the mantra possesses nineteen syllables, ending with the beloved of Agni.
Its sage is Varāha, the metre is Nivṛt-Gāyatrī and so forth;

the deity is Dharaṇī, the bīja is the praṇava, the śakti is the beloved of Vasu.
The arrangement of limbs is made with syllables numbering three, four, three, five, two, and nine.

One should meditate on the divine Dharaṇī as dark-complexioned, adorned with varied ornaments,
seated on a lotus, having high and firm breasts, holding in her hands two blue lotuses, a sheaf of rice, and a parrot,

and wearing garments of varied colors.
Having meditated thus, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times, and one-tenth thereof with milk-rice

mixed with clarified butter the mantra-practitioner should offer into fire, and should worship on the seat of Viṣṇu.
Having conceived a form by means of the root-mantra, he should worship Vasumatī in it.

Having first worshipped the limbs, and having worshipped earth, fire, water, and wind
upon the directional petals, and her powers upon the corner petals,

1.70.s:
nivṛttiśca pratiṣṭā ca vidyānāṃ taiśca tatkalāḥ /
indrādyānapi vajrādīnpūjayettadanantaram //
pūrnaṃ siddhe manau mantrī sādhayediṣṭamātmanaḥ /
dharaṇīṃ prabhajannevaṃ paśuratnāṃbarādibhiḥ //
dharaṇyā vallabhaḥ sa syātsukhī jīvecchataṃ samā /
trailokyamohano mantro jagannāthasya kīrtyate //
tāraḥ kāmo ramā bījaṃ hṛdante puruṣottamaḥ /
śrīkaṇṭhaḥ pratirūpānte lakṣmīti ca nivāsiṃ ca //
sakalānte jagatpaścātkṣobhaṇeti padaṃ vadet /
sarvastrīhṛdayānte tu vidāraṇapadaṃ vadet //
tatastribhuvanāntaṃ tu madonmādakareti ca /
surāsurānte manujasuṃdarījanavarṇataḥ //
manāṃsi tāpayadvandvaṃ dīpayadvitayaṃ tataḥ /
śoṣayadvitayaṃ paścānmārayadvitayaṃ tataḥ //
staṃbhayadvitayaṃ bhūyo mohayadvitaya tataḥ /
drāvayadvitayaṃ tāvadākarṣayayugaṃ tataḥ //
1.70.d:
निवृत्तिश्च प्रतिष्टा च विद्यानां तैश्च तत्कलाः ।
इन्द्राद्यानपि वज्रादीन्पूजयेत्तदनन्तरम् ॥
पूर्नं सिद्धे मनौ मन्त्री साधयेदिष्टमात्मनः ।
धरणीं प्रभजन्नेवं पशुरत्नांबरादिभिः ॥
धरण्या वल्लभः स स्यात्सुखी जीवेच्छतं समा ।
त्रैलोक्यमोहनो मन्त्रो जगन्नाथस्य कीर्त्यते ॥
तारः कामो रमा बीजं हृदन्ते पुरुषोत्तमः ।
श्रीकण्ठः प्रतिरूपान्ते लक्ष्मीति च निवासिं च ॥
सकलान्ते जगत्पश्चात्क्षोभणेति पदं वदेत् ।
सर्वस्त्रीहृदयान्ते तु विदारणपदं वदेत् ॥
ततस्त्रिभुवनान्तं तु मदोन्मादकरेति च ।
सुरासुरान्ते मनुजसुंदरीजनवर्णतः ॥
मनांसि तापयद्वन्द्वं दीपयद्वितयं ततः ।
शोषयद्वितयं पश्चान्मारयद्वितयं ततः ॥
स्तंभयद्वितयं भूयो मोहयद्वितय ततः ।
द्रावयद्वितयं तावदाकर्षययुगं ततः ॥
1.70.m:
namely, Nivṛtti, Pratiṣṭhā, Vidyā, and their parts,
immediately after that he should worship Indra and the others, as well as the vajra and other weapons.

When the mantra is completely mastered, the mantra-practitioner achieves his desired aim.
Thus honoring Dharaṇī with cattle, gems, garments, and other things,

he becomes dear to the earth and shall live happily for a hundred years.
Now the mantra of Jagannātha that bewilders the three worlds is proclaimed:

The praṇava, the Kāma-bīja, Ramā's bīja, Puruṣottama following hṛt,
Śrīkaṇṭha followed by pratirūpa, and lakṣmī and nivāsi,

after sakala one should utter the word jagat, then kṣobhaṇa;
after sarvastrīhṛdaya one should utter the word vidāraṇa;

then following tribhuvana, madonmādakara;
after surāsura, through the syllables manujasundarījana,

then manāṃsi, two tāpayas, then a pair of dīpayas,
then a pair of śoṣayas, then a pair of mārayas,

again a pair of stambhayas, then a pair of mohayas,
then a pair of drāvayas, then a pair of ākarṣayas,

1.70.s:
samastaparamo yena subhagena ca saṃyutam /
sarvasaubhāgyaśabdānte karasarvapadaṃ vadet //
1.70.d:
समस्तपरमो येन सुभगेन च संयुतम् ।
सर्वसौभाग्यशब्दान्ते करसर्वपदं वदेत् ॥
1.70.m:
samastaparama, joined with subhaga,
after the word sarvasaubhāgya one should utter the words kara and sarva,

1.70.s:
kāmapradādamunbrahmāseṃdurhanuyugaṃ tataḥ /
cakreṇa gadayā paścātkhaḍgena tadanantaram //
1.70.d:
कामप्रदादमुन्ब्रह्मासेंदुर्हनुयुगं ततः ।
चक्रेण गदया पश्चात्खड्गेन तदनन्तरम् ॥
1.70.m:
kāmaprada, adamu, the letter na with anusvāra, then a pair of hanus,
with the cakra, with the mace, after that with the sword,

1.70.s:
sarvabāṇairbhediyugaṃ pāśenānte kaṭadvayam /
aṅkuśeneti saṃprocya tāḍayadvitayaṃ punaḥ //
1.70.d:
सर्वबाणैर्भेदियुगं पाशेनान्ते कटद्वयम् ।
अङ्कुशेनेति संप्रोच्य ताडयद्वितयं पुनः ॥
1.70.m:
with all arrows, a pair of bhedis, with the noose, followed by two kaṭas,
having pronounced 'with the elephant-goad', again a pair of tāḍayas,

1.70.s:
kuruśabdadvayamatho kiṃ tiṣṭasi padaṃ vadet /
tāvadyāvatpadasyānte samāhitamanantaram /
tato me siddhirābhāsya bhavamante ca varma phaṭ //
1.70.d:
कुरुशब्दद्वयमथो किं तिष्टसि पदं वदेत् ।
तावद्यावत्पदस्यान्ते समाहितमनन्तरम् ।
ततो मे सिद्धिराभास्य भवमन्ते च वर्म फट् ॥
1.70.m:
then a pair of the word kuru, one should utter the word kiṃ tiṣṭhasi,
then as far as the word yāvat, followed by samāhita,
then having revealed me siddhi, at the end of the vocative form varma and phaṭ,

1.70.s:
hṛdanto 'yaṃ mahāmantro dviśatārṇaḥ samīritaḥ /
jaiminirmunirasyoktaśchandaścāmitamīritam //
1.70.d:
हृदन्तो ऽयं महामन्त्रो द्विशतार्णः समीरितः ।
जैमिनिर्मुनिरस्योक्तश्छन्दश्चामितमीरितम् ॥
1.70.m:
this great mantra ending with hṛt is declared to contain two hundred syllables.
Its sage is said to be Jaimini, and its metre is said to be Amita;

1.70.s:
devatā jagatāṃ mohe jagannāthaḥ prakīrtitaḥ /
kāmo bījaṃ ramā śaktirviniyogo 'khilāptaye //
1.70.d:
देवता जगतां मोहे जगन्नाथः प्रकीर्तितः ।
कामो बीजं रमा शक्तिर्विनियोगो ऽखिलाप्तये ॥
1.70.m:
the deity for enchanting the worlds is proclaimed as Jagannātha;
the Kāma-bīja is the seed, Ramā is the śakti, and the application is for obtaining all things.

1.70.s:
puruṣottamatribhuvanonmādakānte 'gnivarma ca /
hṛdayaṃ kīrtitaṃ paścājjagatkṣobhaṇaśabdataḥ //
1.70.d:
पुरुषोत्तमत्रिभुवनोन्मादकान्ते ऽग्निवर्म च ।
हृदयं कीर्तितं पश्चाज्जगत्क्षोभणशब्दतः ॥
1.70.m:
After puruṣottamatribhuvanonmādaka, the fire-armour (svāhā)
is proclaimed as the heart; next, after the word jagatkṣobhaṇa,

1.70.s:
lakṣmīdayitavarmāntaḥ śiraḥ proktaṃ śikhā punaḥ /
manmatho tamaśabdānte maṅgaje padamīrayet //
1.70.d:
लक्ष्मीदयितवर्मान्तः शिरः प्रोक्तं शिखा पुनः ।
मन्मथो तमशब्दान्ते मङ्गजे पदमीरयेत् ॥
1.70.m:
ending in lakṣmīdayitavarma is declared the head; again, the crest-lock:
after the word manmathottama, one should utter the words maṅgaje,

1.70.s:
kāmadāyeti huṃ procya nyasedvama tataḥ param /
paramānte bhṛgukarṇābhyāṃ ca sarvapadaṃ tataḥ //
1.70.d:
कामदायेति हुं प्रोच्य न्यसेद्वम ततः परम् ।
परमान्ते भृगुकर्णाभ्यां च सर्वपदं ततः ॥
1.70.m:
having pronounced kāmadāya hūṃ, one should assign the armour thereafter;
after parama, through the ears of Bhṛgu, and then the word sarva,

1.70.s:
saubhāgyakaravarmānte kavacaṃ pārikīrtitam /
surāsurānte manujasuṃdarīti padaṃ vadet //
1.70.d:
सौभाग्यकरवर्मान्ते कवचं पारिकीर्तितम् ।
सुरासुरान्ते मनुजसुंदरीति पदं वदेत् ॥
1.70.m:
ending in saubhāgyakaravarma, the armour is proclaimed;
after surāsura, one should utter the word manujasundarī,

1.70.s:
hṛdayānte vidā paścādraṇasarvapadaṃ vadet /
tataḥ praharaṇadharasarvakāmukatatpadam //
1.70.d:
हृदयान्ते विदा पश्चाद्रणसर्वपदं वदेत् ।
ततः प्रहरणधरसर्वकामुकतत्पदम् ॥
1.70.m:
after hṛdaya, then the words vidāraṇa and sarva;
then that word praharaṇadharasarvakāmuka,

1.70.s:
hanayugmaṃ ca hṛdayaṃ bandhanāni tato vadet /
ākarṣayadvayaṃ paścānmahābalapadaṃ tataḥ //
1.70.d:
हनयुग्मं च हृदयं बन्धनानि ततो वदेत् ।
आकर्षयद्वयं पश्चान्महाबलपदं ततः ॥
1.70.m:
a pair of hanas and the heart, then one should utter bandhanāni,
then a pair of ākarṣayas, then the word mahābala,

1.70.s:
varma cāstraṃ samākhyātaṃ netraṃ syāttadanantaram /
vadetribhuvanaṃ paścāccara sarvajaneti ca //
1.70.d:
वर्म चास्त्रं समाख्यातं नेत्रं स्यात्तदनन्तरम् ।
वदेत्रिभुवनं पश्चाच्चर सर्वजनेति च ॥
1.70.m:
and varma and the weapon are declared; immediately after that should be the eye:
one should say tribhuvana, and next cara sarvajana,

1.70.s:
manāṃsi harayugmānte dārayadvitayaṃ ca me /
vaśamānaya varmānte netramantraḥ samīritaḥ //
1.70.d:
मनांसि हरयुग्मान्ते दारयद्वितयं च मे ।
वशमानय वर्मान्ते नेत्रमन्त्रः समीरितः ॥
1.70.m:
manāṃsi, after a pair of haras, two dārayas, and me
vaśam ānaya ending in varma is proclaimed as the eye mantra.

1.70.s:
ṣaḍaṅgamantrāstārādyāḥ phaṭnamontāḥ prakīrtitāḥ /
tārastrailokyaśabdānte mohaneti padaṃ vadet //
1.70.d:
षडङ्गमन्त्रास्ताराद्याः फट्नमोन्ताः प्रकीर्तिताः ।
तारस्त्रैलोक्यशब्दान्ते मोहनेति पदं वदेत् ॥
1.70.m:
The six limb-mantras are proclaimed as beginning with the praṇava and ending in phaṭ and namaḥ.
The praṇava, after the word trailokya, one should utter the word mohana,

1.70.s:
hṛṣīkeśeti saṃprocyāpratirūpādiśabdataḥ /
mamnathānantaraṃ sarvastrīṇāṃ hṛdayamīrayet //
1.70.d:
हृषीकेशेति संप्रोच्याप्रतिरूपादिशब्दतः ।
मम्नथानन्तरं सर्वस्त्रीणां हृदयमीरयेत् ॥
1.70.m:
having pronounced hṛṣīkeśa, from the word apratirūpa and so on,
after manmatha, one should utter sarvastrīṇāṃ hṛdayam,

1.70.s:
ākarṣaṇapadā gacchadāgacchahṛdayāntimaḥ /
anena vyāpakaṃ kṛtvā jagannāthaṃ smaret sudhīḥ //
1.70.d:
आकर्षणपदा गच्छदागच्छहृदयान्तिमः ।
अनेन व्यापकं कृत्वा जगन्नाथं स्मरेत् सुधीः ॥
1.70.m:
followed by the word ākarṣaṇa, ending in gacchāgacchahṛdaya.
Having performed the pervasive placement with this, the wise person should remember Jagannātha:

1.70.s:
kṣīrābdhestu taṭe ramyaṃ suradrumalatāñcitam /
udyadarkābhujālābhaṃ svadhāmnojvāladiṅmukham //
1.70.d:
क्षीराब्धेस्तु तटे रम्यं सुरद्रुमलताञ्चितम् ।
उद्यदर्काभुजालाभं स्वधाम्नोज्वालदिङ्मुखम् ॥
1.70.m:
On the pleasant shore of the ocean of milk, graced with creepers of divine trees,
having the radiance of the network of the rays of the rising sun, illuminating the directions with his own splendour,

1.70.s:
prasūnāvalisaurabhyamādyanmadhukarāravam /
divyavātoñcalatkañjaparāgoddhūlitāṃbaram //
1.70.d:
प्रसूनावलिसौरभ्यमाद्यन्मधुकरारवम् ।
दिव्यवातोञ्चलत्कञ्जपरागोद्धूलितांबरम् ॥
1.70.m:
resounding with intoxicated bees fragrant with clusters of blossoms,
with the atmosphere dusted with the pollen of lotuses stirred by divine breezes,

1.70.s:
svarvadhūgītamādhuryābhirāma cintayedvanam /
tadantarmaṇisampattisphurattoraṇamaṇḍape //
1.70.d:
स्वर्वधूगीतमाधुर्याभिराम चिन्तयेद्वनम् ।
तदन्तर्मणिसम्पत्तिस्फुरत्तोरणमण्डपे ॥
1.70.m:
one should contemplate the delightful grove with the sweetness of the songs of celestial damsels;
within that, in a pavilion with arched doorways shining with an abundance of jewels,

1.70.s:
vilasanmauktikoddāmadāmarājadvitānake /
maṇivedyādi viyatkirīṭāgrasamarcite //
1.70.d:
विलसन्मौक्तिकोद्दामदामराजद्वितानके ।
मणिवेद्यादि वियत्किरीटाग्रसमर्चिते ॥
1.70.m:
under a canopy resplendent with rows of shining, large pearls,
honoured with jewelled altars and the like, reaching to the sky with its crown,

1.70.s:
divyasiṃhāsane vipra samāsīnaṃ smaredvibhum /
śaṅkhapāśeṣu cāpāni musalaṃ nandakaṃ gadām //
1.70.d:
दिव्यसिंहासने विप्र समासीनं स्मरेद्विभुम् ।
शङ्खपाशेषु चापानि मुसलं नन्दकं गदाम् ॥
1.70.m:
the wise one should meditate on the Lord seated upon a divine lion-throne, O brahmin,
holding with his arms the conch, noose, bow, pestle, Nandaka sword, mace,

1.70.s:
aṅkuśaṃ dadhataṃ dorbhiḥ śliṣṭe kamalayorasi /
paśyatyaṅkasthayāṃbhojaśriyā rāgollasadṛśā //
1.70.d:
अङ्कुशं दधतं दोर्भिः श्लिष्टे कमलयोरसि ।
पश्यत्यङ्कस्थयांभोजश्रिया रागोल्लसदृशा ॥
1.70.m:
and elephant-goad, embraced by Kamalā on his chest,
looking upon Lotus-Śrī seated upon his lap with eyes sparkling with affection.

1.70.s:
dhyātvaivaṃ prajapellakṣacatuṣkaṃ taddaśāṃśataḥ /
kuṇḍer'ddhacandre padmairvā jātīpuṣpaiśca homayet //
1.70.d:
ध्यात्वैवं प्रजपेल्लक्षचतुष्कं तद्दशांशतः ।
कुण्डेर्ऽद्धचन्द्रे पद्मैर्वा जातीपुष्पैश्च होमयेत् ॥
1.70.m:
Having thus meditated, one should recite [the mantra] four hundred thousand times; one-tenth thereof
one should offer into fire in a crescent-shaped pit with lotuses or jasmine flowers.

1.70.s:
yāgabhūmiṃ tathātmānaṃ yāgopakaraṇaṃ tathā /
pūjayiṣyan jagannāthaṃ gāyatryā prokṣayedvudhaḥ //
1.70.d:
यागभूमिं तथात्मानं यागोपकरणं तथा ।
पूजयिष्यन् जगन्नाथं गायत्र्या प्रोक्षयेद्वुधः ॥
1.70.m:
Intending to worship Jagannātha, the wise person should sprinkle with the gāyatrī
the sacrificial ground, himself, and the sacrificial implements.

1.70.s:
trailokyamohanāyānte vidmahe padamīrayet /
smarāya dhīmahītyuktvā tanno viṣṇuḥ pracodayāt //
1.70.d:
त्रैलोक्यमोहनायान्ते विद्महे पदमीरयेत् ।
स्मराय धीमहीत्युक्त्वा तन्नो विष्णुः प्रचोदयात् ॥
1.70.m:
After trailokyamohanāya, one should utter the word vidmahe;
having said smarāya dhīmahi, [then] tanno viṣṇuḥ pracodayāt.

1.70.s:
gāyatryeṣā samākhyātā sarvaśuddhikarī parā /
kalpayedāsanaṃ pīṭhe pūrvokte vaiṣṇave sudhīḥ //
1.70.d:
गायत्र्येषा समाख्याता सर्वशुद्धिकरी परा ।
कल्पयेदासनं पीठे पूर्वोक्ते वैष्णवे सुधीः ॥
1.70.m:
This is proclaimed as the supreme gāyatrī that purifies everything.
The wise one should arrange the seat on the previously described Vaiṣṇava pīṭha.

1.70.s:
pakṣirājāya ṭhadvandvaṃ pīṭhamantro 'yamīritaḥ /
mūrtiṃ saṃkalpamūlena tasyāmāvāhayedataḥ //
1.70.d:
पक्षिराजाय ठद्वन्द्वं पीठमन्त्रो ऽयमीरितः ।
मूर्तिं संकल्पमूलेन तस्यामावाहयेदतः ॥
1.70.m: "To the king of birds [Garuḍa], svāhā"—this is stated as the mantra of the ritual seat. / Then, with the root [mantra], having formed the conception, one should invoke the form [of the deity] upon it.

1.70.s:
vyāpakanyāsamantreṇa tataḥ sampūjya bhaktitaḥ /
śrīvatsahṛdayaṃ tena śrīvatsaṃ stanayoryajet //
1.70.d:
व्यापकन्यासमन्त्रेण ततः सम्पूज्य भक्तितः ।
श्रीवत्सहृदयं तेन श्रीवत्सं स्तनयोर्यजेत् ॥
1.70.m: Then, having worshipped with devotion through the mantra of pervasive ritual placement, / one should worship the Śrīvatsa on the breasts with that [mantra] having Śrīvatsa in the heart [i.e., ending with namaḥ].

1.70.s:
kaustubhāya hṛdantena yajedvakṣasi kaustubham /
pūjayedvanamālāyai hṛdantena gale ca tām //
1.70.d:
कौस्तुभाय हृदन्तेन यजेद्वक्षसि कौस्तुभम् ।
पूजयेद्वनमालायै हृदन्तेन गले च ताम् ॥
1.70.m: One should worship the Kaustubha on the chest with [the mantra ending in] the heart for Kaustubha. / And one should worship the forest garland on the neck with [the mantra ending in] the heart for the forest garland.

1.70.s:
karṇikāyāṃ tato 'bhyarcayedvidhivañcāṅgadevatāḥ /
daleṣu pūjayetpaścāllakṣmyādyāvṛttacāmarāḥ //
1.70.d:
कर्णिकायां ततो ऽभ्यर्चयेद्विधिवञ्चाङ्गदेवताः ।
दलेषु पूजयेत्पश्चाल्लक्ष्म्याद्यावृत्तचामराः ॥
1.70.m: Then one should worship the deities of the limbs on the pericarp according to rule. / Afterwards, on the petals, one should worship Lakṣmī and the others who hold fly-whisks,

1.70.s:
bandhūkakusumābhāsāḥmuktāhāralasatkucāḥ /
utphullāṃbhaghojanayanā madavibhramamantharāḥ //
1.70.d:
बन्धूककुसुमाभासाःमुक्ताहारलसत्कुचाः ।
उत्फुल्लांभघोजनयना मदविभ्रममन्थराः ॥
1.70.m: shining like bandhūka flowers, their breasts radiant with pearl necklaces, / their eyes like blossoming lotuses, languid with the amorous play of passion:

1.70.s:
lakṣmī sarasvatī caiva dhṛtiḥ prītistataḥ param /
kāntiḥ śāntistuṣṭipuṣṭibījādyā ṅenamontikāḥ //
1.70.d:
लक्ष्मी सरस्वती चैव धृतिः प्रीतिस्ततः परम् ।
कान्तिः शान्तिस्तुष्टिपुष्टिबीजाद्या ङेनमोन्तिकाः ॥
1.70.m: Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, and Dhṛti, and after that Prīti, / Kānti, Śānti, Tuṣṭi, and Puṣṭi, beginning with their seed-syllables and ending with the dative and namaḥ.

1.70.s:
bhṛguḥ khaḍrāśacandrāḍhyo devyā bījamudāhṛtam /
hrasvatrayaklībasarvarahitasvarasaṃyutam //
1.70.d:
भृगुः खड्राशचन्द्राढ्यो देव्या बीजमुदाहृतम् ।
ह्रस्वत्रयक्लीबसर्वरहितस्वरसंयुतम् ॥
1.70.m: Bhṛgu [sa], combined with kha [ha], ra, and the moon [candrabindu, producing srāṃ etc.], is declared as the seed-syllable of the goddess, / joined with the vowels devoid of the three short vowels and all neuter vowels.

1.70.s:
devyā bījaṃ kramādāsāmādau ca viniyojayet /
dalāgreṣu yajecchaṅkhaṃ śārṅgaṃ cakramasiṃ gadām //
1.70.d:
देव्या बीजं क्रमादासामादौ च विनियोजयेत् ।
दलाग्रेषु यजेच्छङ्खं शार्ङ्गं चक्रमसिं गदाम् ॥
1.70.m: One should employ the seed-syllable of the goddess at the beginning of these in order. / At the tips of the petals, one should worship the conch, the bow Śārṅga, the discus, the sword, the mace,

1.70.s:
aṅkuśaṃ musalaṃ pāśaṃ svamudrāmanubhiḥ pṛthak /
mahājalacarā yānte varmāstraṃ vahnivallabhā //
1.70.d:
अङ्कुशं मुसलं पाशं स्वमुद्रामनुभिः पृथक् ।
महाजलचरा यान्ते वर्मास्त्रं वह्निवल्लभा ॥
1.70.m: the goad, the pestle, and the noose, separately, with their own mudrās and mantras: / "O great aquatic creature," followed by "yā", the armor [huṃ], the weapon [phaṭ], and the beloved of fire [svāhā],

1.70.s:
pāñcajanyā pratārādyo namontaḥ śaṅkhapūjane /
śārṅgāya saśayānte ca varmāstraṃ vahnivallabhā //
1.70.d:
पाञ्चजन्या प्रताराद्यो नमोन्तः शङ्खपूजने ।
शार्ङ्गाय सशयान्ते च वर्मास्त्रं वह्निवल्लभा ॥
1.70.m: preceded by the star [Oṃ], [followed by] "To Pāñcajanya," ending with namaḥ, in the worship of the conch; / "To the bow Śārṅga," ending with "saśa", the armor [huṃ], the weapon [phaṭ], and the beloved of fire [svāhā];

1.70.s:
śārṅgāya hṛdayaṃ mantro mahādyaḥ śārṅgapūjane /
sudarśanamahānte tu cakrarājapadaṃ vadet //
1.70.d:
शार्ङ्गाय हृदयं मन्त्रो महाद्यः शार्ङ्गपूजने ।
सुदर्शनमहान्ते तु चक्रराजपदं वदेत् ॥
1.70.m: "To the bow Śārṅga, namaḥ" is the mantra beginning with mahat in the worship of the Śārṅga; / and after "O great Sudarśana," one should utter the word "king of discuses",

1.70.s:
hayayugmaṃ sarvaduṣṭabhayamante kurudvayam /
chindhidvayaṃ tataḥ paścādvidārayayugaṃ tataḥ //
1.70.d:
हययुग्मं सर्वदुष्टभयमन्ते कुरुद्वयम् ।
छिन्धिद्वयं ततः पश्चाद्विदारययुगं ततः ॥
1.70.m: the pair "haya", "fear to all wicked ones," ending with the two "kuru"s; / then the two "chindhi"s, and then the pair "vidāraya";

1.70.s:
paramantrān grasadvandvaṃ bhakṣayadvitayaṃ punaḥ /
bhūkāni trāsayadvandvaṃ varmaphaḍvahnisuṃdarī //
1.70.d:
परमन्त्रान् ग्रसद्वन्द्वं भक्षयद्वितयं पुनः ।
भूकानि त्रासयद्वन्द्वं वर्मफड्वह्निसुंदरी ॥
1.70.m: "swallow the mantras of others" twice, again the two "bhakṣaya"s, / "terrify the beings" twice, the armor [huṃ], phaṭ, and the beauty of fire [svāhā];

1.70.s:
sudarśanāya hṛdayaṃ proktaścakrarcane manuḥ /
mahākhaḍgatīkṣṇapadācchiviyugmaṃ samīrayet //
1.70.d:
सुदर्शनाय हृदयं प्रोक्तश्चक्रर्चने मनुः ।
महाखड्गतीक्ष्णपदाच्छिवियुग्मं समीरयेत् ॥
1.70.m: "To Sudarśana, namaḥ" is declared as the mantra in the worship of the discus. / After the words "O sharp great sword," one should utter the pair "chindhi",

1.70.s:
huṃ phaṭ svāhā ca khaḍgāya namaḥ khaḍgārcane manuḥ /
mahākaumodakītyante vadeñcaiva mahābale //
1.70.d:
हुं फट् स्वाहा च खड्गाय नमः खड्गार्चने मनुः ।
महाकौमोदकीत्यन्ते वदेञ्चैव महाबले ॥
1.70.m: huṃ phaṭ svāhā, and "To the sword, namaḥ" is the mantra in the worship of the sword. / After "O great Kaumodakī," one should utter, "O immensely powerful one,

1.70.s:
sarvāsurāntake paścātprasīdayugaleti ca /
varmāstravahnijāyāntakaumodaki hṛkṣatimaḥ //
1.70.d:
सर्वासुरान्तके पश्चात्प्रसीदयुगलेति च ।
वर्मास्त्रवह्निजायान्तकौमोदकि हृक्षतिमः ॥
1.70.m: destroyer of all asuras," and then the pair "be pleased"; / ending with the armor [huṃ], the weapon [phaṭ], and the wife of fire [svāhā], "To Kaumodakī, namaḥ"—

1.70.s:
kaumodakyarcane prokto mantraḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ /
mahāṅkuśapadātkuṭcayugmaṃ huṃphaṭvasupriyā //
1.70.d:
कौमोदक्यर्चने प्रोक्तो मन्त्रः सर्वार्थसाधकः ।
महाङ्कुशपदात्कुट्चयुग्मं हुंफट्वसुप्रिया ॥
1.70.m: this is declared as the mantra accomplishing all aims in the worship of Kaumodakī. / After the word "great goad," the pair "kuṭa", huṃ phaṭ, and the beloved of the Vasus [svāhā];

1.70.s:
aṅkuśāya namaḥ prokto mantragrauvākuśarcane /
saṃvartakamahānte tu musaleti padaṃ vadet //
1.70.d:
अङ्कुशाय नमः प्रोक्तो मन्त्रग्रौवाकुशर्चने ।
संवर्तकमहान्ते तु मुसलेति पदं वदेत् ॥
1.70.m: "To the goad, namaḥ" is declared as the mantra in the worship of the great goad. / After "the great Saṃvartaka," one should utter the word "pestle",

1.70.s:
yodhayadvitayaṃ varma phaḍante vahnisuṃdarī /
musalāya namaḥ prokto mantro susalapūjane //
1.70.d:
योधयद्वितयं वर्म फडन्ते वह्निसुंदरी ।
मुसलाय नमः प्रोक्तो मन्त्रो सुसलपूजने ॥
1.70.m: the two "yodhaya"s, the armor [huṃ], followed by phaṭ, and the beauty of fire [svāhā]; / "To the pestle, namaḥ" is declared as the mantra in the worship of the pestle.

1.70.s:
mahāpāśa hadādaghaṭayamākarṣayadvayam /
huṃ phaṭe svāhā ca pāśāya namaḥ pāśārcane manuḥ //
1.70.d:
महापाश हदादघटयमाकर्षयद्वयम् ।
हुं फटे स्वाहा च पाशाय नमः पाशार्चने मनुः ॥
1.70.m: After the words "great noose," the pair "ākarṣaya" [attract], / huṃ phaṭ svāhā, and "To the noose, namaḥ" is the mantra in the worship of the noose.

1.70.s: tārādyā manavo hyete tataḥ śakrādikānyajet //
1.70.d: ताराद्या मनवो ह्येते ततः शक्रादिकान्यजेत् ॥
1.70.m: These mantras indeed begin with the star [Oṃ]. Then one should worship Indra and the other [guardians of the quarters].

1.70.s:
vajrādyānapi saṃpūjya sarvasiddhīśvaro bhavet /
māsamātraṃ tu kusumaiḥ pūjayitvā hayārijaiḥ //
1.70.d:
वज्राद्यानपि संपूज्य सर्वसिद्धीश्वरो भवेत् ।
मासमात्रं तु कुसुमैः पूजयित्वा हयारिजैः ॥
1.70.m: Having worshipped the thunderbolt and the other weapons as well, one becomes the lord of all supernatural powers. / Having worshipped for only a month with oleander flowers,

1.70.s:
kumudairvā prajuhuyādaṣṭottarasahasrakam /
māsamātreṇa vaśyāḥsyustasya sarve nṛpottamāḥ //
1.70.d:
कुमुदैर्वा प्रजुहुयादष्टोत्तरसहस्रकम् ।
मासमात्रेण वश्याःस्युस्तस्य सर्वे नृपोत्तमाः ॥
1.70.m: or having made fire oblations of a thousand and eight white water lilies, / within only a month all the best of kings become subject to his will.

1.70.s:
yasya nāma yutaṃ mantraṃ japedayutasaṃkhyayā /
sa bhaveddāsavatsadyo mantrasyāsya prabhāvataḥ //
1.70.d:
यस्य नाम युतं मन्त्रं जपेदयुतसंख्यया ।
स भवेद्दासवत्सद्यो मन्त्रस्यास्य प्रभावतः ॥
1.70.m: If one recites the mantra joined with a person's name for a myriad of times [ten thousand], / that person instantly becomes like a servant by the power of this mantra.

1.70.s:
bahunā kimihoktena manunānena sādhakaḥ /
sādhayetsakalānkāmānviṣṇutulyo na saṃśayaḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne tṛtīyapāde saptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.70.d:
बहुना किमिहोक्तेन मनुनानेन साधकः ।
साधयेत्सकलान्कामान्विष्णुतुल्यो न संशयः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने तृतीयपादे सप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः
1.70.m:
What is the use of speaking much here? By this mantra the practitioner / can accomplish all desires, equal to Viṣṇu, without doubt.

Thus ends the seventieth chapter in the third quarter of the great narrative in the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.71.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi divyānnaraharermanūn /
yānsamārādhya brahmādyāścakruḥ sṛṣṭyādi karma vai //
1.71.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
शृणु नारद वक्ष्यामि दिव्यान्नरहरेर्मनून् ।
यान्समाराध्य ब्रह्माद्याश्चक्रुः सृष्ट्यादि कर्म वै ॥
1.71.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Listen, O Nārada: I shall proclaim the divine mantras of the Man-Lion, / by worshipping which Brahmā and the others indeed performed actions such as creation.

1.71.s:
saṃvartakaścandramaulirmanurvahnivibhūṣitaḥ /
