1.73.m: Meditating on him slaying Meghanāda, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times; / he swiftly conquers a great host of enemies, even one difficult to conquer.

1.73.s:
dhyātvā śūrpaṇakhānāsāchedanodyuktamānasam /
sahasraṃ prajapenmantraṃ puruhūtādikān jayet //
1.73.d:
ध्यात्वा शूर्पणखानासाछेदनोद्युक्तमानसम् ।
सहस्रं प्रजपेन्मन्त्रं पुरुहूतादिकान् जयेत् ॥
1.73.m: Meditating on his mind resolved on cutting off the nose of Śūrpaṇakhā, / one should recite the mantra a thousand times; he conquers Indra and the other [gods].

1.73.s:
rāmapādābjasevārthaṃ kṛtodyogamatho smaran /
prajapallaṅkṣamekānte mahārogātpramucyate //
1.73.d:
रामपादाब्जसेवार्थं कृतोद्योगमथो स्मरन् ।
प्रजपल्लङ्क्षमेकान्ते महारोगात्प्रमुच्यते ॥
1.73.m: Then, remembering him resolved upon serving the lotus feet of Rāma, / reciting [it] one hundred thousand times in solitude, one is freed from grave disease.

1.73.s:
trimāsaṃ vijitāhāro nityaṃ saptasahasrakam /
aṣṭottaraśataiḥ puṣpairniśchedraiḥ śātapatrakaiḥ //
1.73.d:
त्रिमासं विजिताहारो नित्यं सप्तसहस्रकम् ।
अष्टोत्तरशतैः पुष्पैर्निश्छेद्रैः शातपत्रकैः ॥
1.73.m: Conquering one's food for three months, daily [reciting it] seven thousand times, / having worshipped according to the rule with one hundred and eight unblemished hundred-petalled flowers,

1.73.s:
pūjayitvā vidhānena pāyasaṃ ca saśarkaram /
nivedya prajapenmantraṃ kuṣṭarogātpranucyate //
1.73.d:
पूजयित्वा विधानेन पायसं च सशर्करम् ।
निवेद्य प्रजपेन्मन्त्रं कुष्टरोगात्प्रनुच्यते ॥
1.73.m: and having offered rice pudding with sugar, one should recite the mantra; / he is freed from the disease of leprosy.

1.73.s:
vijane vijitāhāraḥ ṣaṇmāsaṃ vidhināmunā /
kṣayarogātpramucyeta satyaṃ satyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ //
1.73.d:
विजने विजिताहारः षण्मासं विधिनामुना ।
क्षयरोगात्प्रमुच्येत सत्यं सत्यं न संशयः ॥
1.73.m: In a secluded place, with diet restrained for six months according to this rule, / one would be freed from consumption; this is true, true, there is no doubt.

1.73.s:
abhimantrya jalaṃ prātarmantreṇa triḥ samāhitaḥ /
trisaṃdhyaṃ vā pibennityaṃ mucyate sarvarogataḥ //
1.73.d:
अभिमन्त्र्य जलं प्रातर्मन्त्रेण त्रिः समाहितः ।
त्रिसंध्यं वा पिबेन्नित्यं मुच्यते सर्वरोगतः ॥
1.73.m: Having consecrated water with the mantra three times in the morning with concentration, / or drinking it daily at the three junctions of the day, one is freed from all diseases.

1.73.s:
dāridrayaṃ ca parābhūtaṃ jāyate dhanadopamaḥ /
viṣādidoṣasaṃsparśo na bhavettu kadācana //
1.73.d:
दारिद्रयं च पराभूतं जायते धनदोपमः ।
विषादिदोषसंस्पर्शो न भवेत्तु कदाचन ॥
1.73.m: Poverty is overcome, and he becomes equal to the giver of wealth [Kubera]; / no contact with blemishes such as poison ever occurs.

1.73.s:
manunā mantritaistoyaiḥ pratyehaṃ kṣālayenmukham /
mukhanetrādisaṃbhūtāñjayeddvrogāṃśca dāruṇān //
1.73.d:
मनुना मन्त्रितैस्तोयैः प्रत्येहं क्षालयेन्मुखम् ।
मुखनेत्रादिसंभूताञ्जयेद्द्व्रोगांश्च दारुणान् ॥
1.73.m: One should wash the face every day with water consecrated with the mantra; / he overcomes terrible diseases arising in the mouth, eyes, and other [organs].

1.73.s:
pītvābhimantritaṃ tvaṃbhaḥ kukṣirogān jayeddhruvam /
lakṣmaṇapratimāṃ kṛtvā dadyādbhaktyā vidhānataḥ //
1.73.d:
पीत्वाभिमन्त्रितं त्वंभः कुक्षिरोगान् जयेद्ध्रुवम् ।
लक्ष्मणप्रतिमां कृत्वा दद्याद्भक्त्या विधानतः ॥
1.73.m: Drinking water consecrated with the mantra, he will certainly conquer diseases of the belly. / Having fashioned an image of Lakṣmaṇa, one should give it with devotion according to rule.

1.73.s:
sa sarvebhyo 'tha rogebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ /
kanyārthī vimalāpāṇigrahaṇāsaktamānasaḥ //
1.73.d:
स सर्वेभ्यो ऽथ रोगेभ्यो मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ।
कन्यार्थी विमलापाणिग्रहणासक्तमानसः ॥
1.73.m: He is freed from all diseases, there is no doubt in this. / A man desiring a maiden, whose mind is set upon taking her pure hand in marriage,

1.73.s:
dhyāyan lakṣaṃ japenmantrī abjairhutvā daśāṃśataḥ /
īpsitāṃ labhate kanyāṃ śīgrameva na saṃśayaḥ //
1.73.d:
ध्यायन् लक्षं जपेन्मन्त्री अब्जैर्हुत्वा दशांशतः ।
ईप्सितां लभते कन्यां शीग्रमेव न संशयः ॥
1.73.m: meditating, should recite a hundred thousand [times] as a practitioner, offering one-tenth into the fire with lotuses; / he obtains the desired maiden very quickly, there is no doubt.

1.73.s:
dīkṣitaṃ juṃbhaṇāstrāṇāṃ mantreṣu niyatavratam /
dhyātvā ca vidhivannityaṃ japenmāsatrayaṃ manum //
1.73.d:
दीक्षितं जुंभणास्त्राणां मन्त्रेषु नियतव्रतम् ।
ध्यात्वा च विधिवन्नित्यं जपेन्मासत्रयं मनुम् ॥
1.73.m: Meditating on him as initiated into the mantras of the stupor-inducing weapons, observing fixed vows, / one should daily recite the mantra according to rule for three months,

1.73.s:
pūjāpuraḥsaraṃ saptasahasraṃ vijitendriyaḥ /
sarvāsāmapi vidyānāṃ tattvajño jāyate naraḥ //
1.73.d:
पूजापुरःसरं सप्तसहस्रं विजितेन्द्रियः ।
सर्वासामपि विद्यानां तत्त्वज्ञो जायते नरः ॥
1.73.m: preceded by worship, seven thousand [times], with senses conquered; / that man becomes a knower of the truth of all sciences.

1.73.s:
viśvāmitrakratuvare kṛtādbhutaparākramam /
dhyāyaṃllakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ mucyate mahato bhayāt //
1.73.d:
विश्वामित्रक्रतुवरे कृताद्भुतपराक्रमम् ।
ध्यायंल्लक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं मुच्यते महतो भयात् ॥
1.73.m: Meditating on him whose valor was wonderful in the excellent sacrifice of Viśvāmitra, / reciting the mantra a hundred thousand times, one is freed from great danger.

1.73.s:
kṛtanityakriyaḥ śuddhastrikālaṃ prajapenmanum /
sarvapāpavinirmukto yāti viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam //
1.73.d:
कृतनित्यक्रियः शुद्धस्त्रिकालं प्रजपेन्मनुम् ।
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो याति विष्णोः परं पदम् ॥
1.73.m: Having performed the daily rites, purified, reciting the mantra at the three junctures of the day, / released from all sins, he goes to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

1.73.s:
dīkṣito vidhivanmantrī guṇairvigatakalmaṣaḥ /
svācāraniyato dānto gṛhastho vijitendriyaḥ //
1.73.d:
दीक्षितो विधिवन्मन्त्री गुणैर्विगतकल्मषः ।
स्वाचारनियतो दान्तो गृहस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.73.m: An initiated practitioner according to rule, free from defilement by virtues, / devoted to his own proper conduct, subdued, a householder with senses conquered,

1.73.s:
aihikānanapekṣyaiva niṣkāmo yor'cayedvibhum /
sa sarvānpuṇyapāpaudhāndagdhvā nirmalamānasaḥ //
1.73.d:
ऐहिकाननपेक्ष्यैव निष्कामो योर्ऽचयेद्विभुम् ।
स सर्वान्पुण्यपापौधान्दग्ध्वा निर्मलमानसः ॥
1.73.m: who worships the Lord without desire, disregarding worldly rewards, / having burned the entire mass of merits and sins, with a purified mind,

1.73.s:
punarāvṛttirahitaḥ śāśvataṃ padamaśvataṃ padamaśnute /
sakāmo vāñchitān labdhvā bhuktvā bhogān manogatān //
1.73.d:
पुनरावृत्तिरहितः शाश्वतं पदमश्वतं पदमश्नुते ।
सकामो वाञ्छितान् लब्ध्वा भुक्त्वा भोगान् मनोगतान् ॥
1.73.m: free from rebirth, attains the eternal abode. / One with desires, having obtained the sought-after [ends] and enjoyed the pleasures desired in his mind,

1.73.s:
jātiramaraściraṃ bhūtvā yāti viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam /
nidrācandrānvitā paścādbharatāya hṛdantimaḥ //
1.73.d:
जातिरमरश्चिरं भूत्वा याति विष्णोः परं पदम् ।
निद्राचन्द्रान्विता पश्चाद्भरताय हृदन्तिमः ॥
1.73.m: becomes long-lived and free from old age, and goes to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu. / [The syllable] ‘nidrā’ combined with the moon, then ‘bharatāya’, and ending with ‘hṛt’—

1.73.s:
saptākṣaro manuścāsya munyādyarcādi pūrvavat /
bakaḥ seṃduśca śatrudhnaparaṃ ṅetaṃ hṛdantimaḥ //
1.73.d:
सप्ताक्षरो मनुश्चास्य मुन्याद्यर्चादि पूर्ववत् ।
बकः सेंदुश्च शत्रुध्नपरं ङेतं हृदन्तिमः ॥
1.73.m: this is his seven-syllabled mantra; its sage and the rest, and worship, are as before. / ‘Baka’ with the moon, followed by ‘śatrughna’ in the dative, and ending with ‘hṛt’—

1.73.s:
saptākṣaro 'yaṃ śatrudhnamantraḥ sarveṣṭasiddhidaḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge buhadupākhyāne sanatkumāravibhāge tṛtīyapāde rāmādyupāsanāvarṇanaṃ nāma trisaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.73.d:
सप्ताक्षरो ऽयं शत्रुध्नमन्त्रः सर्वेष्टसिद्धिदः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बुहदुपाख्याने सनत्कुमारविभागे तृतीयपादे रामाद्युपासनावर्णनं नाम त्रिसप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः
1.73.m:
this is the seven-syllabled Śatrughna mantra, granting the fulfillment of all desires.

Thus in the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa, in the first part, in the great narrative, in the section of Sanatkumāra, in the third quarter, the seventy-third chapter, entitled ‘Description of the Worship of Rāma and Others’.
